复制为 Markdown 入门 最后验证时间：2026-10-20。 Announced September 16, 2026. The merged experience rolled out gradually, starting with Pro and Max on web, desktop and mobile, then Team and Free; Enterprise organizations got at least 30 days' notice. Update — October 8, 2026: Claude Docs, Claude Slides and Claude Design left beta and are available on every plan, including Free, on by default (on Enterprise they turned on by default on October 15, 2026). Two further templates, Dashboards and Motion, arrived in beta the same day — see Dashboards & Motion. Check the Help Center article for current status before relying on anything here. 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. On September 16, 2026, Anthropic collapsed three products into one. Chat, Cowork (the agentic workspace) and Claude Design stopped being separate places you had to choose between. There is now one conversation box, and Claude decides what the task needs. The official framing is short: "Ask Claude for what you need, and it can decide which tool to use." The practical consequence is longer, and it is what this page is about — because a merge like this moves settings, retires habits, and ships two new document tools whose limits are not obvious until you hit them. What you'll learn Understand what actually merged on September 16, 2026 — and why 'no mode to choose' changes how you open a task Find every setting that moved: global instructions, web search, research, and file storage Pick correctly between Claude Docs, Claude Slides, Claude Design, a plain artifact, and a downloaded .docx/.pptx Use Claude Docs the way it's designed: tabs, inline comments, @Claude edits, and real-time co-authoring Know the eight limits that will bite you — no version history, no comment-only role, charts that don't refresh, and the compliance configurations where Docs is simply unavailable Predict the usage-limit cost of agentic work now that everything runs in one conversation
documents.s: One Claude: The Merge, Claude Docs & Claude Slides

documents.t: Nothing you had is thrown away. Per Anthropic: "Existing Cowork tasks, projects, connectors, skills, artifacts, and files carry over, and those Cowork tasks open as they did before, so you can continue them." What changes is the entry point. Previously you decided the shape of the work before you described it — chat for a question, Cowork for a project. Now you describe the work and Claude picks the machinery, with the same context, skills and connectors available from any conversation.

This is the part that generates the most "where did my button go" confusion, and it is the part no third-party write-up covers. Four things relocated: What you used Where it is now Global instructions Settings → General Web search toggle Gone — it's automatic. Claude decides when to search Research Type /deep-research, or use the + button Your files Settings → Storage folder Watch out The web-search toggle is not hidden, it is removed. If your workflow depended on forcing search off for a private or offline-reasoning task, that lever no longer exists in the UI — say it in the prompt instead ('answer from the conversation only; do not search the web').

The merge shipped Claude Docs and Claude Slides as new tools, and moved Claude Design inside conversations. All three are templates — a starting shape for an artifact, not a separate app. Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Claude Docs — living documents⌄ Rich-text documents saved to your Claude account, with headings, tables and other formatting, and more than one tab (like sections of a notebook). You and Claude and your colleagues all write in the same document, at the same time. Exports to Word (.docx), PDF, Markdown (.md) and Google Docs. Reach for it when the document itself is the deliverable and it will keep changing. ←PreviousNext→ 2Claude Slides — presentations⌄ Decks built from your notes, a report, or the work already in the conversation. You can edit any slide directly, present without leaving Claude, and export to PowerPoint and PDF. Reach for it when you need a deck out of material you already produced. ←PreviousNext→ 3Claude Design — visuals and prototypes⌄ Visuals, mockups, prototypes, one-pagers and landing pages, built against your design system. Exports as a .zip, PDF, PowerPoint, or standalone HTML. Reach for it when the output is visual or needs to match a brand. ←PreviousNext→ 4A plain artifact — code, apps, charts⌄ Still there, unchanged, on every plan including Free. A runnable mini-app, a chart, a diagram, a script. Reach for it when the thing needs to execute rather than be read. See Artifacts. ←PreviousNext→ 5A generated file — .docx / .pptx / .xlsx / .pdf⌄ A one-shot file Claude builds and you download. No live editing surface, no sharing, no comments. Reach for it when you need a file to hand off and never touch inside Claude again. See Generating Real Files. ←PreviousNext→ The distinction that matters most is the last two: a Claude Doc is a living document with a URL, collaborators and comments; a generated .docx is a download. If you asked for "a Word doc" pre-merge and got a file, asking the same way now may get you a Doc you then export — which is usually what you wanted, but it is a different object with different sharing rules.
documents.s: The three templates: which one do you actually want?

documents.t: Guided walkthrough1 of 3 1Ask in any conversation⌄ Plain language is enough — 'turn the plan we just worked through into a product spec I can share with the team.' Claude asks a few questions before it starts, then drafts the doc on screen. ←PreviousNext→ 2Choose a template explicitly⌄ Select Output in the message box and choose a template. Use this when Claude keeps picking a different shape than you want. ←PreviousNext→ 3Start from the Artifacts tab⌄ Pick a template from the gallery, then brief Claude. Useful when the document, not the conversation, is the thing you came for. ←PreviousNext→ Brief a Claude Doc so the first draft is close CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ Create a Claude Doc: a one-page product spec for the export feature we just designed. Structure it in four tabs: 1. Summary — problem, proposed solution, who it's for 2. Requirements — numbered, testable, each with a rationale 3. Open questions — things I still need to decide, with your recommendation and the tradeoff for each 4. Rejected alternatives — what we considered and why not Rules: - Pull the decisions from this conversation. Do not invent requirements I did not state. - Where I was vague, leave a comment asking me the question instead of guessing. - Add a table comparing the three export formats we discussed. Ask me anything you need before you start drafting.

Three editing paths coexist, which is the point of the tool: You type. Click into the doc and type. Changes save automatically. You ask. Request a change conversationally; Claude edits and explains what it did and why. You comment. Select text and leave a comment for your collaborators — and mention @Claude in a comment to have Claude make that edit in place. Claude replies in the thread, makes the change, and explains it. Claude also leaves its own comments while drafting, to explain a choice or ask you a question. This is the behavior worth designing your prompt around: telling Claude to ask in a comment rather than guess (as in the prompt card above) converts silent hallucination risk into a visible question you can answer. You can also ask Claude to add a chart, diagram, graph or timeline to a doc.

People with edit access work on the same doc at the same time as you and Claude, and everyone's edits appear in real time. Viewer Editor Read ✅ ✅ Edit ❌ ✅ Comment ❌ ✅ Export ❌ ✅ Sharing rules differ sharply by plan: Pro / Max — share with anyone who has the link. Team / Enterprise — invite specific people or a group, or share with everyone in your organization. Docs cannot be shared outside your organization, by link or by email invitation. Either way — opening a shared doc requires a Claude account, and only the owner can rename or delete a doc.
Docs work on web, desktop, Claude Code, and mobile — but the iOS and Android apps are view-only: no editing and no template selection from a phone. Plan around that if your review loop is mobile.

Every one of these is documented, and every one surprises somebody in week one. Guided walkthrough1 of 9 1No version history yet⌄ There is no way to see or restore an earlier state of a doc. Anyone with edit access can overwrite anything, and your only recovery is an export you took earlier. For a document that matters, export to Markdown at each milestone until history ships. ←PreviousNext→ 2No comment-only access level⌄ The roles are viewer and editor, nothing between. A reviewer who should comment but not edit does not exist as a permission — grant edit and rely on trust, or grant view and collect feedback elsewhere. ←PreviousNext→ 3Charts and diagrams don't update automatically⌄ A chart Claude added is a snapshot. Change the underlying numbers in the doc and the chart keeps showing the old ones until you ask Claude to regenerate it. Treat every visual as stale until re-asked. ←PreviousNext→ 4Team and Enterprise cannot share externally⌄ No link sharing, no email invitation outside the organization. If you need to send a doc to a client, export it (Word, PDF, Markdown, Google Docs) and send the export. ←PreviousNext→ 5Mobile is view-only⌄ iOS and Android can read a doc. They cannot edit one or pick a template. ←PreviousNext→ 6Unavailable under CMEK, ZDR and HIPAA⌄ Claude Docs is not available for organizations configured with customer-managed encryption keys, zero data retention, or HIPAA. This is the single most important fact for regulated teams, and it is not a rollout delay — it is an exclusion. ←PreviousNext→ 7Not in the Compliance API yet⌄ Activity inside a doc is not recorded in the Compliance API. If your audit posture depends on that export, doc activity is currently a blind spot. ←PreviousNext→ 8The standalone Claude Design site closes December 14, 2026⌄ If your team used the standalone site, migrate design systems from the Artifacts page before then — chats, comments and public project links from the standalone version are deleted when it closes. Full checklist on Dashboards & Motion. ←PreviousNext→ 9The newer templates still have the Enterprise toggle⌄ Docs, Slides and Design are now on by default everywhere, including Enterprise as of October 15, 2026. The two beta templates are not: Dashboards and Motion are off on Enterprise until an owner turns each one on in organization settings, under Artifacts. ←PreviousNext→
documents.s: The limits that will bite you

documents.t: The unified experience does not yet support GitHub integration ("Add from GitHub"), conversation branching, search across older Cowork tasks, Dispatch (existing users only), or incognito chats for file and code creation. If your workflow leans on branching or on searching your Cowork history, that capability is temporarily gone — not moved.
documents.s: Also not supported yet in the merged experience

documents.t: There is no separate price. The relevant sentence is about usage limits: "Everything you do with Claude counts toward your plan's usage limits. Longer agentic tasks that search the web, run code, or create files generally use more than a quick question." Claude Docs counts the same way. The merge makes this sharper than it sounds. Previously, opening Cowork was a deliberate act — you knew you were starting expensive work. Now a casually-phrased request in the same box can trigger a long agentic run that searches, executes code and writes files. The cost signal moved from the door to the prompt. If you are on a plan where limits matter, say what you want explicitly: Keep a request cheap when you only want an answer CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ Answer from this conversation only. Do not search the web, do not run code, and do not create any files or artifacts. Two paragraphs. And the inverse, when you do want the full machinery: Ask for the expensive version on purpose CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ Take this as a full task, not a chat answer. Research the three vendors below, check their current pricing pages, build a comparison spreadsheet, and turn the recommendation into a Claude Doc I can share with the team. Cite every figure with a link and the date you read it. Vendors: [A], [B], [C]

Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Re-home your global instructions⌄ They moved to Settings → General. Open them once and re-read them: instructions written for chat-only Claude ('you cannot browse the web', 'ask before doing anything long') can now actively fight the merged behavior. ←PreviousNext→ 2Stop reaching for the web-search toggle⌄ It's gone. Put search intent in the prompt — either 'check current sources' or 'do not search'. ←PreviousNext→ 3Relearn research⌄ Type /deep-research or use the + button. It is a command now, not a mode. ←PreviousNext→ 4Audit anything that assumed Cowork was separate⌄ Scheduled tasks, connectors and skills carried over, but prompts that said 'this is a Cowork task' as a signal to work harder no longer signal anything. Replace that framing with explicit scope, as in the prompt cards above. ←PreviousNext→ 5Decide your Docs export cadence⌄ Until version history ships, pick a milestone rhythm — export to Markdown whenever the doc reaches a state you would be upset to lose. ←PreviousNext→

Check yourself 0/4 Key takeaways One conversation, no mode to choose: the cost signal moved from the door (opening Cowork) to the prompt. Say explicitly when you want a cheap answer and when you want the full agentic run. Four things moved: global instructions → Settings → General; web search → automatic, steer in the prompt; research → /deep-research or +; files → Settings → Storage folder. A Claude Doc is a living document with collaborators and comments; a generated .docx is a download. Choose deliberately — they share rules differ completely. Design your prompt around Claude's comments: tell it to ask in a comment rather than guess, and you convert invention into a visible question. Two limits deserve a workaround today: no version history (export to Markdown at milestones) and charts that never refresh (regenerate after every data change). Regulated teams: Claude Docs is unavailable under CMEK, ZDR and HIPAA, and doc activity is not in the Compliance API yet.

documents.t: 消费级方案会限制你在一个时间窗口内能用多少（消息/用量会随时间重置），更高层级会提高这些上限。当你触及限额时，通常会被要求等待其重置或进行升级——你的工作不会丢失，只是暂停一下。 更重的模型（以及更长的对话）会更快消耗你的额度。如果你频繁触及限额，一个快速的解决办法是为新话题开启全新的对话，并让提示词保持聚焦（与上下文管理是同一个思路）。
**从 Free 开始。**搞清楚你实际用它来做什么。 当限额打断真实工作时，升级到 Pro。 如果你是仍然触及上限的重度用户，就升级到 Max。 当同事需要共享访问、管理或合规时，选择 Team/Enterprise。

**有依据的回答。**添加你的文档（一本手册、规格说明、笔记），Claude 便会基于它们作答——这是 RAG 的一种内置、无需写代码的形态。 **持久的上下文。**项目指令的作用就像一个限定范围的系统提示词，覆盖其中的一切。 **井然有序。**关于同一个主题/客户/计划的所有对话都集中在一起。
创建一个项目，并赋予它清晰的用途。 添加知识——它应当始终知晓的文件/文本。 编写项目指令——角色、约定、该做什么/避免什么。 开始聊天——每一次对话都会继承这些知识 + 指令。
一个客户/账户工作区（他们的文档 + 你的笔记）。 一个用于问答的代码库或产品知识库。 一个带有你的风格指南和过往作品的写作项目（让草稿契合你的语气）。 为某门课程学习，加载好教学大纲和材料。
精选知识——相关、最新的文件胜过把一切都倒进去（噪音会损害检索效果）。 让指令精炼且准确（与自定义指令是同一条规则）。 不要添加你不愿意存储的敏感数据——参见隐私。

Exact settings paths, plan availability, and what the recap surfaces can change — check Settings and the help center for current behavior. 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. What you'll learn Understand what Claude Reflect surfaces in your monthly recap — and what it doesn't See why it depends on memory being switched on Configure break reminders and quiet hours under Time and focus Weigh the genuine privacy trade-off before you turn it on Know how to read usage insights without letting them nudge you On July 9, 2026, Claude added two quietly personal features: Reflect (a monthly recap of how you use Claude) and Time and focus settings (break reminders and quiet hours). They're small in surface area but worth understanding, because they sit on top of your memory and shape how much of your usage Claude analyzes about you.

Reflect lives at Settings → Reflect. Once a month it surfaces: the topics you spent time on, your most active day and peak hour, and observations about how you work with Claude. It's in beta on Free, Pro, and Max, on the web and Claude Desktop. Watch out Reflect requires memory to be enabled. That's the key dependency: the recap is generated from what Claude retains about your conversations. No memory, no recap — and turning memory on to get the recap means Claude is also carrying facts about you across chats. Decide on the memory trade-off first; the recap is downstream of it.

Separately, Settings → Time and focus lets you configure optional break reminders and quiet hours to manage your own work patterns. These are nudges you opt into — a reminder to step away, and windows where Claude won't prompt you. Guided walkthrough1 of 4 1Turn on memory (if you want Reflect)⌄ Reflect is generated from memory, so enable it first — or skip Reflect entirely and use only Time and focus. ←PreviousNext→ 2Open Settings → Reflect⌄ On web or Claude Desktop, enable the monthly recap (beta). ←PreviousNext→ 3Read your first recap critically⌄ Treat topics, peak hour, and 'observations' as a mirror, not a scoreboard. ←PreviousNext→ 4Set Time and focus⌄ Under Settings → Time and focus, add break reminders and quiet hours that match how you actually want to work. ←PreviousNext→
documents.s: Time and focus: break reminders and quiet hours

documents.t: Usage-insight features are useful and also, by design, engagement-shaped: a recap that celebrates your "most active day" is a mirror, but it can also be a nudge to come back. Reporting on Reflect's launch framed it as quietly encouraging more AI use. That's not a reason to avoid it — it's a reason to read it deliberately. Pro tip A healthy way to use Reflect: skim the topics to notice where your attention actually went, ignore the streak-and-peak framing, and let quiet hours — not a recap — decide when you step away. The insight is the value; the gamification is optional.

Don't confuse the distinct things Claude calls "memory-adjacent": Feature What it does Needs memory on? Memory Carries facts about you across chats — (it is memory) Reflect Monthly recap of topics, peak time, work observations Yes Time and focus Break reminders and quiet hours No Projects Scoped context for a body of work No Check yourself 0/3 Key takeaways Reflect (Settings → Reflect) gives a monthly recap of topics, most active day, peak hour, and work observations — beta on Free, Pro, Max, web + Desktop. It requires memory to be enabled, because the recap is built from what Claude retains about you. Time and focus (break reminders, quiet hours) is separate and does not need memory. Usage recaps are engagement-shaped by design — read the topics as a mirror and let quiet hours, not streaks, govern your breaks.

documents.t: 在路上捕捉灵感——把一个杂乱的想法说出来；请 Claude 把它结构化。 免手动的时刻——走路、通勤、做饭。 练习与头脑风暴——出声地来回交流感觉很自然。 无障碍——对许多人来说，说话可能比打字更轻松（参见无障碍）。

复制为 Markdown 入门 最后验证时间：2026-07-15。 Screen reader mode, vimInsertModeRemaps, and fullscreen mouse-click support shipped in Claude Code v2.1.208 (July 14, 2026). Flag names, setting keys, and behavior can change between releases — confirm in the official changelog and settings docs. 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. Claude Code runs in the terminal — a text UI, which is a good starting point for accessibility, but the default rendering leans on color, box-drawing glyphs, and spinners that screen readers and some motor setups handle poorly. As of July 2026 there's a dedicated screen reader mode plus settings for vim ergonomics and mouse/scroll behavior. This page collects the levers that make the CLI usable with assistive tech. What you'll learn How to turn on screen reader mode — three ways, and what each changes What screen reader mode actually does to the transcript, tables, and permission prompts How to remap vim insert-mode keys (jj → Escape) to reduce hand strain How to control or disable mouse clicks and scroll acceleration in fullscreen Where high-contrast themes live, and how to report an accessibility gap

Screen reader mode swaps the decorative TUI for a plain-text rendering that assistive tech can read cleanly. Turn it on any of three ways — a one-off flag, an environment variable for every session, or a persistent setting. Guided walkthrough1 of 3 1Try it for one session⌄ Launch with the flag: claude --ax-screen-reader. Nothing else changes — same session, plainer output. ←PreviousNext→ 2Turn it on for every session⌄ Export the environment variable CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1 in your shell profile so it applies everywhere. ←PreviousNext→ 3Make it permanent in settings⌄ Set "axScreenReader": true in a settings.json file (user-level ~/.claude/settings.json applies to all projects). ←PreviousNext→ Persistent screen reader mode (~/.claude/settings.json) CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ { "axScreenReader": true }

Pro tip Plain-text rendering replaces the styled TUI so screen readers get clean, linear text. Decorative glyphs are hidden from screen readers instead of being read out as noise. Transcript symbols are announced as short labels rather than raw characters. Nested tables are read as Header: value. lines — flattened into speakable rows. Permission mode changes are announced aloud when you cycle modes with Shift+Tab. That last one matters: cycling permission modes with Shift+Tab is a core Claude Code interaction (see Permissions), and screen reader mode speaks the new mode aloud so you always know whether you're in plan, accept-edits, or auto mode without reading the status line.

If you use vim mode and reaching for Escape strains your hand, map a two-key insert-mode sequence to it instead. The vimInsertModeRemaps setting turns sequences like jj into Escape, so you never leave the home row. Map jj to Escape in vim mode (settings.json) CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ { "editorMode": "vim", "vimInsertModeRemaps": { "jj": "Escape" } } Watch out The remap only fires in insert mode, so typing jj as literal text needs a brief pause between keys — pick a sequence you rarely type fast (jj and kj are common choices). editorMode: vim enables vim keybindings; vimInsertModeRemaps only takes effect while vim mode is on.

Fullscreen menus now accept mouse clicks — including multi-select menus and the "Other" input rows — which helps if keyboard-only navigation is painful. Two settings tune pointer behavior for motion sensitivity or precision: Setting What it does CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS Disables mouse click, drag, and hover while keeping wheel scroll — useful if stray clicks disrupt you. wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled Set to false to turn off mouse-wheel scroll acceleration in fullscreen, for steadier, predictable scrolling. Steadier scrolling, no accidental clicks (settings.json) CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ { "wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled": false, "env": { "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS": "1" } }

For low-vision users, terminal contrast is the first lever. Claude Code ships light and dark themes and supports custom themes you build from /theme or ship in a plugin — so you can dial in a high-contrast palette that meets your needs. See Settings for where theme choice is stored, and Output Styles if you also want plainer, less-decorated prose (the Explanatory and Learning styles are more verbose, not less — for terse output stay on Default). Beyond the CLI Screen reader mode covers the terminal. For hands-free interaction with Claude more broadly, Voice Mode in the app lets you talk and listen, and the Accessibility playbook covers using Claude itself as an assistive tool — simplifying text, building checklists, and adapting information to how you read. Check yourself 0/3 Pro tip Screen reader mode: --ax-screen-reader flag (once), CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1 (per shell), or axScreenReader: true (persistent). It plain-texts the transcript, hides decorative glyphs, flattens tables, and speaks permission-mode changes on Shift+Tab. vimInsertModeRemaps eases hand strain; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS and wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled tune pointer behavior. Custom themes give you high-contrast palettes; Voice Mode and the Accessibility playbook cover the rest.

复制为 Markdown 高级 What you'll learn The six steps the Agent SDK walks for every tool call, in order Which steps can only deny, which can only allow, and which can do both — the mental model that makes the rest obvious Why a tool approved early never reaches your canUseTool callback, and what to use instead when a check must run on every call The five configurations where allowedTools looks like a lock and isn't How deny rules differ when you name a tool versus scope a pattern inside it What a subagent inherits — and the one mode it refuses to inherit The circuit breaker no rule, mode, or hook can override Most people configure an agent's permissions the way they'd configure a firewall: write the rules, assume the most specific one wins. The Claude Agent SDK does not work that way. It walks a fixed six-step pipeline for every tool call, and each step has a different power — some can only block, some can only approve, and only two can do either. Get the order wrong and you ship an agent that looks locked down and isn't. This is the most common class of harness bug, and it is almost never a typo in a rule. 最后验证时间：2026-10-21。 The evaluation order, mode behaviors, and version gates below are from Anthropic's Agent SDK permissions reference and the permission-modes reference. Permission surfaces change often and several behaviors are gated on specific Claude Code versions (noted inline) — re-check both pages before relying on a carve-out. 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源.
documents.s: Agent SDK Permissions: the Six-Step Order

documents.t: Guided walkthrough1 of 6 1Hooks⌄ Your PreToolUse hook runs first, before every other check. A hook deny is final — it blocks the call even in bypassPermissions mode. A hook allow, by contrast, is not final: steps 2 and 3 still run. ←PreviousNext→ 2Deny rules⌄ From disallowedTools and settings.json. A match blocks the call in every mode, bypassPermissions included. ←PreviousNext→ 3Ask rules⌄ From settings.json. A match does not approve or block — it routes the call down to step 6, your callback, even in bypassPermissions mode. ←PreviousNext→ 4Permission mode⌄ The active mode gets its say here. bypassPermissions approves what reaches it; acceptEdits approves in-scope file operations; plan forces file-edit and shell-write tools down to your callback regardless of allow rules. Other modes fall through. ←PreviousNext→ 5Allow rules⌄ From allowedTools and settings.json. A match approves the call. Calls the tool approves on its own resolve here too, with no rule needed — a file read inside your working directories, a read-only Bash command. ←PreviousNext→ 6canUseTool⌄ Anything still unresolved reaches your callback for a decision. In dontAsk mode this step is skipped and the call is denied. ←PreviousNext→

Forget precedence. Ask instead: what is this step allowed to do? Step Can deny Can approve Can route to your callback 1. Hooks Yes — final, survives bypassPermissions Yes, but steps 2–3 still run — 2. Deny rules Yes — final, survives bypassPermissions No — 3. Ask rules No No Yes — survives bypassPermissions 4. Permission mode No Yes (bypassPermissions, acceptEdits) Yes (plan, for writes) 5. Allow rules No Yes No 6. canUseTool Yes Yes — Three consequences fall straight out of that table, and they explain nearly every surprise: Deny beats everything. Deny rules and hook denials sit upstream of the mode, so there is no mode that unlocks them. This is the only mechanism you can rely on to remove capability. Allow beats nothing. Allow rules sit at step 5, below the mode. They cannot restrict a permissive mode — they only pre-approve work that would otherwise have prompted. Your callback is the last resort, not the gate. It runs only on calls nothing above it resolved. Every check you put inside it is skipped for anything approved earlier. Watch out If you are writing security checks inside canUseTool, you have put them in the wrong place. A call approved by an allow rule, by acceptEdits, or by bypassPermissions never reaches the callback — your check does not fail, it simply does not run. Checks that must apply to every call belong in a PreToolUse hook, which runs at step 1 and whose denial survives even bypassPermissions.
documents.s: The model that makes it make sense

documents.t: allowedTools reads like an allowlist. It is a pre-approval list. Anything you leave off it is still available to Claude; it just falls through to the mode and then to your callback. Five specific traps:
documents.s: Five ways allowedTools isn't a lock

documents.t: This is the big one. Unlisted tools match no allow rule, so they fall through to step 4 — where bypassPermissions approves them. Looks locked down. Approves Bash, Write, and Edit. CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ // WRONG — bypassPermissions approves everything unlisted const options = { allowedTools: ["Read"], permissionMode: "bypassPermissions" }; If you need bypassPermissions but want specific tools gone, the only lever that works is disallowedTools — it lands at step 2, upstream of the mode.

To get "these tools and nothing else," pair the pre-approval with a mode that denies instead of prompting. A read-only agent, for real CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ const options = { allowedTools: ["Read", "Glob", "Grep"], permissionMode: "dontAsk" }; Listed tools run. Anything else that would have prompted is denied, and canUseTool is never called. Note what still runs without being listed: read-only Bash commands, file reads inside your working directories, and tools like Agent that don't ask before running. To remove one of those from the request entirely, add its bare name to disallowedTools.
documents.s: 2. dontAsk is the mode that makes an allowlist exact

documents.t: Coverage depends on the entry's shape, and the difference is large: Entry What it pre-approves "Read" Every Read call (except reads from network paths) "Bash(npm test *)" Only matching Bash calls. Other Bash calls still fall through to your callback Scoping is the whole game. "Bash" on an allow list is a different security posture from "Bash(npm test *)", and the type system will not tell you.
documents.s: 3. A bare name approves the whole tool

documents.t: Allow rules accept tool-name globs only after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix, and the server segment must be glob-free. Entry Effect "mcp__puppeteer__*" Works — every tool from the puppeteer server "mcp__github__get_*" Works — that server's get_ tools "*" or "mcp__*" Ignored. Pre-approves nothing The last row fails open in the quiet direction — you get more prompts, not fewer permissions — but if you wrote it expecting a blanket approval, you will spend an afternoon on it.

If you pass a canUseTool callback in a configuration where the SDK knows the callback will be shadowed, it emits a one-time Node process warning with the code CLAUDE_SDK_CAN_USE_TOOL_SHADOWED. Two configurations trigger it: permissionMode: "bypassPermissions", and each bare allowedTools entry such as "Read". Surface the shadowing warning in your own logs CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ process.on("warning", (w) => { if (w.code === "CLAUDE_SDK_CAN_USE_TOOL_SHADOWED") { console.error("[harness] canUseTool will be skipped:", w.message); } }); Scoped entries like Bash(ls *) and acceptEdits mode don't trigger it, and allow rules coming from settings files are invisible to the check — so a clean run is not proof your callback is reachable.
documents.s: 5. TypeScript warns you, on a channel you aren't listening to

documents.t: Deny entries behave differently depending on their shape, and the difference is about what Claude can see, not just what it can do. Entry Effect disallowedTools: ["Bash"] The Bash tool definition is removed from the request. Claude never sees the tool and cannot attempt it disallowedTools: ["Bash(rm *)"] Bash stays available. Calls matching rm * as written are denied in every mode. Other Bash calls — including /bin/rm — fall through disallowedTools: ["*"] Every tool definition is removed. Tool-name globs are supported in deny rules: "mcp__*" matches every MCP tool across all servers Two things to internalize. First, the bare form is strictly stronger: removing the tool from context beats denying its calls, because a tool Claude can't see generates no failed attempts and no retries down a different path. Second, Bash(rm *) matches the string as written — the /bin/rm gap is not a bug, it is the documented scope of a textual rule. Treat scoped Bash denials as guardrails against the obvious, never as a security boundary.
documents.s: Deny rules: naming a tool vs. scoping inside it

documents.t: Scoped Read and Edit rules take a path pattern, and two details catch everyone: Edit(path) governs every built-in tool that writes files — including Write and NotebookEdit. A Write(path) rule is never matched by the file permission checks. If you wrote Write(//secrets/**) you wrote nothing. A double slash means the filesystem. Edit(//secrets/**) blocks writes anywhere under /secrets on disk. A single leading slash anchors at the rule's source instead — for a rule passed through allowedTools or disallowedTools, that's the session's working directory, so Edit(/secrets/**) does not protect /secrets on disk. Block writes to a real filesystem path CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ // // = absolute filesystem path. One slash anchors at the rule's source. const options = { disallowedTools: ["Edit(//etc/**)", "Edit(//secrets/**)", "Read(//secrets/**)"] };
documents.s: Path rules: four anchors and one dead letter

documents.t: Two behaviors worth pinning down because they bite in production: auto mode degrades silently-ish. If you switch to a model auto doesn't support via setModel() or applyFlagSettings(), the session changes to default mode. You get a system message with subtype status and permissionMode: "default" — typed as SDKStatusMessage in TypeScript — and from then on calls reach your callback. Switching the model back does not restore auto; you must call setPermissionMode("auto") again. (v2.1.299 or later.) Subagents inherit, with one refusal. A subagent runs in the parent's permission mode unless you set permissionMode on its AgentDefinition and the parent is in default, dontAsk, or plan. Even then, Claude Code never applies a "bypassPermissions" value from an AgentDefinition — a subagent runs in bypassPermissions only when the parent session itself does (v2.1.267+). That carve-out exists because subagents often have different system prompts and looser behavior than your main agent, so inheriting bypass would hand full autonomous system access to the least-supervised part of your harness. See Subagents.
documents.s: The modes, and what each one actually buys

documents.t: rm and rmdir removals targeting a critical path are never approved by an allow rule or by a PreToolUse hook returning allow. Critical paths are the filesystem root, any direct child of the root (/usr, /etc, /data), your home directory, Windows drive roots and their top-level directories, and your working directory and its parents. A matching deny rule still blocks the command outright; the point is that no approval path can clear it. What happens instead depends on the mode: Mode Outcome for a critical-path removal default, acceptEdits, bypassPermissions Asks for approval auto Asks in the terminal, with a time limit. Elsewhere — including every Agent SDK session — denies it dontAsk Denies it That middle row is the one that matters for a harness: an Agent SDK session in auto mode denies critical-path removals without calling your callback, and tells Claude to report what it wanted to delete instead. If your agent suddenly starts narrating deletions it didn't perform, this is why — not a model regression. The check also reaches inside constructs where an unset variable would expand to a root deletion: rm -rf "$DIR"/*, rm -rf "$1"/* with nothing binding $1, D=$(pwd); rm -rf "$D", and removals nested in subshells, command substitutions, or bash -c scripts. The documented fix is to guard the expansion so the shell errors on empty rather than deleting the root. Make a glob removal pass the critical-path check CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ # Flagged: expands to a removal from / when DIR is unset rm -rf "$DIR"/* # Passes: :? makes the shell exit with an error instead rm -rf "${DIR:?}"/*

Beyond critical-path removals, these always escape a permissive mode — they reach your callback in most modes, and are denied in dontAsk because that mode never prompts: Tools matched by an explicit ask rule AskUserQuestion, and MCP tools whose server sets _meta["anthropic/requiresUserInteraction"] (v2.1.199+) Connector tools your organization set to ask — the callback receives the reason Your organization requires approval for this tool Reads from network paths, which no allow rule approves So "I set bypassPermissions, why am I still being asked?" has four answers before you reach for a bug report. And in the TypeScript SDK there is a fifth lever: permissionPrompts: "none" (v2.1.259+) stops your callback from being called at step 6 entirely — a PermissionRequest hook still gets a chance, and if it declines to decide, the call is denied.

When a check must be unconditional — audit logging, a secret-path scanner, a cost ceiling — put it at step 1. A PreToolUse hook has two ways to block, and both are available to a command hook you can also run outside the SDK: exit code 2, where whatever you wrote to stderr becomes the reason Claude sees, or JSON on stdout with a permissionDecision of "deny" plus a permissionDecisionReason. PreToolUse hook: the only unconditional gate CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ # Runs before deny rules, ask rules, the mode, and allow rules. # A deny here survives bypassPermissions. # Wire it to hooks.PreToolUse in settings.json, or pass it in the SDK's hooks option. jq -e '.tool_input | tostring | test("AKIA|BEGIN PRIVATE KEY|ghp_")' >/dev/null \ && { echo "secret material in tool input" >&2; exit 2; } || exit 0 The in-process callback form the TypeScript and Python SDKs accept returns the same decision fields rather than an exit code. Confirm the wrapper shape against the hooks reference for your SDK version before shipping — the evaluation position is the stable part, the handler signature less so.
documents.s: A gate that actually runs on every call

documents.t: Permission mode is not a one-shot decision. In a streaming session you can start restrictive and loosen it after reviewing the agent's first moves, with set_permission_mode() in Python or setPermissionMode() in TypeScript. The new mode applies immediately to all subsequent tool requests. Start in default, loosen after reviewing the approach CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ const q = query({ prompt: "Refactor the auth module", options: {permissionMode: "default"} }); // ...review the first turns, then: await q.setPermissionMode("acceptEdits"); The inverse is the more interesting move for a long run: tighten to dontAsk once the agent enters a phase that should need no new capability.

Allow, deny, and ask rules can also live declaratively in .claude/settings.json. The SDK reads them when the project setting source is enabled, which it is for default query() options — but if you set settingSources explicitly, you must include "project" or your settings-file rules silently stop applying. This is a classic incident: someone adds settingSources: ["user"] for reproducibility and quietly deletes the project's entire deny list. See Settings for the file precedence, and remember that settings-file allow rules are also invisible to the CLAUDE_SDK_CAN_USE_TOOL_SHADOWED check. Check yourself 0/3 Key takeaways Six steps, fixed order: hooks, deny rules, ask rules, permission mode, allow rules, canUseTool. Deny is upstream of the mode and therefore absolute. Allow is downstream and can only ever pre-approve. allowedTools is a pre-approval list, not an allowlist — pair it with dontAsk to make it exact. Checks in canUseTool do not run for auto-approved calls. Unconditional checks go in a PreToolUse hook. Edit(path) covers Write and NotebookEdit; a Write(path) rule matches nothing. // anchors at the filesystem, a single / at the rule's source. A subagent inherits the parent's mode but never inherits a bypassPermissions value from its own definition. Critical-path rm removals are a circuit breaker no allow rule or hook allow can clear — and an Agent SDK session in auto mode denies them without calling you. Setting settingSources without "project" silently drops every rule in .claude/settings.json.
documents.s: Where the rules can come from

复制为 Markdown 进阶 最后验证时间：2026-06-27。 AGENTS.md 的采用方列表以及 Claude Code 的导入/符号链接行为变化很快——请对照官方 AGENTS.md 站点和 Claude Code 内存文档确认具体细节。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 你已经了解了 CLAUDE.md——Claude Code 的项目说明文件。但你的仓库很可能不止被一个代理触及：队友在用 Codex，CI 用了一个编码机器人，还有人在 Cursor 里打开了这个仓库。AGENTS.md 就是这些工具一致同意会去读取的开放标准，因此你只需编写一次项目说明，而不必为每个工具维护一个不同的文件。 What you'll learn AGENTS.md 是什么、由谁来管理 为什么 Claude Code 读取 CLAUDE.md 而不读 AGENTS.md 在各工具间保持单一可信来源的三种可靠方法 嵌套和全局的 AGENTS.md 文件如何合并 什么内容应该放进文件——什么应该排除在外

AGENTS.md 是位于仓库根目录的一个纯 Markdown 文件——可以把它看作一份写给代理而不是写给人类的 README。它告诉编码代理如何构建、测试和参与该项目。这种格式没有必填字段：代理只是直接读取其中的文字。 它是一个开放标准，由 Linux 基金会下属的 Agentic AI Foundation（AAIF） 管理，截至 2026 年中，已被 6 万多个开源项目使用，并被 30 多个工具读取——包括 OpenAI Codex、Google 的 Jules 和 Gemini CLI、Cursor、Windsurf、Devin、Zed、Warp、Aider、goose、Amp，以及 GitHub Copilot 的编码代理。 What you'll learn AGENTS.md 是一种约定，而不是运行时：每个工具自行决定如何发现、合并和注入该文件。 没有强制的 schema——清晰的文字胜过僵化的结构。 它是对你的 README 的补充；并不取代它。

人们容易踩的地方在于：Claude Code 读取 CLAUDE.md，而不是 AGENTS.md。 如果你的仓库里只有一个 AGENTS.md，Claude Code 默认会忽略它。这不是一个 bug——它早于这个标准出现——但它意味着一个多工具的仓库需要一套刻意的同步策略，否则你的说明会悄悄地相互偏离。 Watch out 不要假设 Claude Code 会回退到 AGENTS.md——它不会自动读取它。 两个手工维护的文件（CLAUDE.md 和 AGENTS.md）会发生偏离。选定一个单一可信来源。 在依赖任何回退说法之前，先在官方内存文档中确认当前行为。

有三种模式能在不重复内容的情况下让 CLAUDE.md 和 AGENTS.md 保持同步。根据你团队的平台来选择。 Guided walkthrough1 of 3 1符号链接（最简单）⌄ 把 CLAUDE.md 做成指向 AGENTS.md 的符号链接。Claude Code 会跟随符号链接并逐字节读取目标文件——只有一个真实文件，零合并逻辑。注意事项：在 Windows 上，创建符号链接需要开发者模式或管理员权限，因此跨平台团队可能更倾向于导入方法。 ←PreviousNext→ 2@import（跨平台）⌄ 保留一个极简的 CLAUDE.md，它唯一的职责就是用 @AGENTS.md 导入来引入标准文件。Claude Code 会在启动时把被导入的文件展开到上下文中，因此 AGENTS.md 仍然是唯一来源，而且在 Windows 上也没有会断掉的符号链接。 ←PreviousNext→ 3/init（迁移）⌄ 在一个已经有 AGENTS.md（或 .cursorrules / .windsurfrules）的仓库里初始化 Claude Code？运行 /init——它会读取那些文件，并把相关部分折叠进一个生成的 CLAUDE.md 中。 ←PreviousNext→ 把 CLAUDE.md 符号链接到共享标准文件（macOS / Linux） CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md 或者保留一个仅一行、用于导入它的 CLAUDE.md CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ @AGENTS.md Pro tip 当你整个团队都在 macOS/Linux 上时，使用符号链接——它需要维护的东西最少。 当团队里有 Windows 贡献者时，使用 @import。 无论你选择哪一种,都把它提交进仓库,这样整个团队都能获得相同的行为。

更完善的代理会以分层方式处理 AGENTS.md——和 CLAUDE.md 内存层级 是同一套心智模型。以 Codex 为例，它会从你主目录中的全局文件出发，向下经过 Git 根目录直到你当前的文件夹，一路拼接： 越靠近实际工作的文件越占上风，因为它们最后被拼接，会覆盖更早的指引。因此 services/payments/AGENTS.md 会继承仓库根目录的说明，并加入仅在该服务内部适用的规则——把专门的指引尽量放在离专门代码最近的地方。
documents.s: 嵌套和全局文件如何合并

documents.t: 和一份好的 CLAUDE.md 是同样的纪律——这个标准只是建议了几个常见的小节： 项目概览——这是什么，两句话讲清。 构建与测试命令——如何运行、测试和检查代码风格。 代码风格——代理无法推断的约定。 测试说明——“完成”意味着什么。 安全注意事项——永远不要触碰或提交什么。 提交 / PR 指南——消息格式、分支规则。 Watch out 代理会逐字遵循该文件——过时或一厢情愿的说明会实实在在地造成伤害，和 CLAUDE.md 完全一样。 保持简短且真实；描述项目当下的实际运作方式。 永远不要提交机密信息；引用大型文档，而不是把它们粘贴进来。

自我检验 0/3 Key takeaways AGENTS.md 是由 Linux 基金会管理、被 30 多个编码代理读取的开放标准——一份写给代理的 README。 Claude Code 读取 CLAUDE.md，而不是 AGENTS.md，因此多工具仓库必须让二者保持同步。 在 Mac/Linux 上把 CLAUDE.md 符号链接到 AGENTS.md，或为跨平台团队使用一行 @AGENTS.md 导入。 嵌套文件按 全局 → 根目录 → 子目录 合并，离得最近的文件占上风。 像填写一份出色的 CLAUDE.md 那样填写它：概览、构建/测试命令、约定、安全和护栏——简短且真实。
CLAUDE.md 与内存文件——同一理念在 Claude Code 一侧的体现 CLAUDE.md 模板——可直接复用为 AGENTS.md 的现成起步模板 斜杠命令——包括用于迁移现有说明文件的 /init

复制为 Markdown 高级 最后验证时间：2026-08-04。 Background-agent defaults changed twice in five weeks (v2.1.198 → v2.1.221) and are still being tuned. Confirm the current commit/push/PR behavior in the Claude Code changelog before wiring a policy around it. 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. On July 1, 2026 Claude Code shipped v2.1.198 and quietly closed the last manual step in the agent loop: background agents launched from claude agents began auto-committing, auto-pushing, and auto-opening a draft PR when they finished code work in a worktree. You went from "here's a task" straight to "here's a reviewable draft" — no keystrokes in the middle. The reaction was immediate and split. Some users loved it; others filed anthropics/claude-code#73197 the next day asking for an off switch so their propose-only workflows (agent proposes, human commits) still worked. Five weeks later, on August 4, 2026, v2.1.221 walked the default back: background sessions now always commit and push to preserve work, but only open a draft PR when the task calls for one. Same primitive, softer default. If you run agents unattended — nightly triage, a /loop on /code-review, a fleet of /forked sessions — this is the workflow you're already inside. Here is what it does end-to-end, what fires when, and how to shape it for your team's trust bar. What you'll learn The exact end-to-end flow from `claude agents` launch to draft PR — commit, push, notification, all of it What v2.1.198 shipped, what v2.1.221 tuned, and why the default softened How `/fork`, `/resume`, `/background`, and (new in v2.1.221) `/subtask` fit around the auto-PR flow The Notification hook payload — `agent_needs_input` vs `agent_completed` — and how to page yourself instead of Claude A propose-only pattern that survives every release by using permissions, not settings, as the enforcement point

The auto-PR flow did not arrive fully-formed — it landed across five releases in six weeks. Reading them in order tells you what each layer of the current behavior is actually for. Date Version Change 2026-07-01 v2.1.198 Subagents run in the background by default. Background agents launched from claude agents auto-commit, auto-push, and auto-open a draft PR on completion. Notification hook fires agent_needs_input and agent_completed for background sessions. 2026-07-15 (approx.) v2.1.212 /fork copies your conversation into a new background session (its own row in claude agents) while you keep working. /resume opens a picker of past sessions, including deleted ones. 2026-07-20 (approx.) v2.1.216 Fix: resumed background sessions restore the agent's prompt and tool restrictions instead of dropping to the default agent. 2026-07-22 (approx.) v2.1.218 /code-review runs as a background subagent by default — review no longer fills the conversation. 2026-08-04 v2.1.221 Default tuned: background sessions always commit and push to preserve work, but open a draft PR only when the task calls for one. In-session subagent that /fork used to launch is now /subtask. Two things worth noticing about that arc: Every step is more autonomy, not less. v2.1.221 did not disable auto-commit or auto-push — it just made the draft PR opt-in-per-task instead of always-on. The runtime still wants your work out of an ephemeral worktree and onto a branch before it forgets. /fork and the auto-PR flow compose. Once a fork is its own row in claude agents, it is a background session — which means when it finishes, the same commit → push → maybe-PR sequence fires. A single /fork launched at lunch can come back as a branch on origin by afternoon.
documents.s: The four shipping events, in order

documents.t: The end-to-end sequence for a claude agents background session on v2.1.221, once its final tool call returns: Guided walkthrough1 of 6 1Worktree stays if there are changes⌄ The runtime keeps the isolated worktree (default location under `~/.claude/worktrees/`) alive as long as the working tree is dirty. If the agent made zero changes, the worktree is pruned automatically — no ghost branches. ←PreviousNext→ 2Commit — always, with the agent's message⌄ The agent writes a commit message summarizing the task and commits every file it touched. This is not a fixup — it is the finished state of the work. ←PreviousNext→ 3Push — always, to a fresh branch⌄ The runtime pushes to a branch (created from the parent HEAD when the worktree was made). This is the step v2.1.221 kept even after tuning: the point is to preserve work off the local machine, not to publish a proposal. ←PreviousNext→ 4Draft PR — only when the task calls for one⌄ Before v2.1.221 the PR always opened. Now the runtime opens a draft PR only if the task itself framed a reviewable change (fix, feature, refactor). Exploratory work or research spawned by `/subtask` pushes but doesn't PR. ←PreviousNext→ 5Notification hook fires⌄ `agent_completed` fires through the `Notification` hook — same channel as `agent_needs_input`, distinguishable by the payload. That's your webhook, your Slack ping, your desk-buzzer moment. ←PreviousNext→ 6Session row updates in `claude agents`⌄ The session moves from Running to Complete in the `claude agents` list, carrying the branch name and (if opened) the PR link. `/resume` can pick it up later with its prompt and tool restrictions intact — the v2.1.216 fix. ←PreviousNext→ The sequence never rolls back. If the push fails (auth, protected branch), the runtime keeps the local commit and surfaces the failure through the same notification — but it will not delete your work.
documents.s: What actually happens when a background agent finishes

documents.t: The two events v2.1.198 added to the Notification hook are the seam where you keep humans in the loop without ever attending the session. Two payload shapes on the same hook CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ # agent_needs_input — session paused waiting for approval or clarification { "event": "agent_needs_input", "session_id": "...", "agent": "code-review", "reason": "..." } # agent_completed — session finished; branch pushed, PR maybe opened { "event": "agent_completed", "session_id": "...", "agent": "feature-x", "branch": "claude/feature-x-2026-08-04", "pr_url": "https://github.com/..." /* or null */ } The pr_url field is the single most useful bit: it is null when the runtime pushed-but-did-not-PR (the v2.1.221 default for exploratory work), and populated when it did. Routing on that field is how you build "only ping me for reviewable work" without a second config layer. A minimal hook that pings a Slack channel only for completions that produced a PR: { "hooks": { "Notification": [ { "matcher": "agent_completed", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "jq -e '.pr_url' >/dev/null && jq -r '\"<\" + .pr_url + \"|Draft PR ready> — \" + .agent' | curl -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d @- $SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" } ] } ] } } The jq -e '.pr_url' gate is the whole trick: -e exits non-zero when the field is missing or null, short-circuiting the rest of the pipeline. Sessions that only committed-and-pushed don't page. Sessions that opened a PR do.
documents.s: The Notification hook — page yourself, not Claude

documents.t: Issue anthropics/claude-code#73197, filed July 2, 2026 — one day after v2.1.198 — asked for a backgroundAgents.autoCreatePr: false in settings.json, or at least separate knobs for commit / push / PR. The reasoning was reasonable: in a "propose-only" workflow the human is the only one allowed to push to origin or open PRs, and a default-on publish step needs an off switch. Anthropic's answer was different in shape. Instead of a new setting, v2.1.221 tuned the default itself (PR only when the task calls for one) and pointed at the existing permission system: a Bash(git push:*) deny rule blocks the push, and a Bash(gh pr create:*) deny rule blocks the PR. The permission layer is authoritative for both interactive and background sessions — it's how the runtime enforces the ban regardless of what the agent decides to do at the end. Watch out There is still no `backgroundAgents.autoCreatePr` key in `settings.json` — 'disable the feature' is spelled with permissions, not settings. A permission deny on `Bash(git push:*)` also blocks the final auto-push, not just interactive pushes. If your only concern is the PR, deny `Bash(gh pr create:*)` instead and let the push through so `/resume` can pick up the branch cleanly. v2.1.221 is the default *today*. If you pin an older Claude Code (2.1.198 – 2.1.220), you get the always-PR behavior — and the permission gate is your only real defense.
documents.s: Why #73197 mattered — and why the fix wasn't a settings key

documents.t: Build the policy at the permission layer, not the settings layer. Then it applies to every session (foreground, background, /fork, /subtask, /loop) and does not care which version of v2.1.x you're on. settings.json — propose-only project policy CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ { "permissions": { "deny": [ "Bash(git push:*)", "Bash(gh pr create:*)", "Bash(gh pr edit:*)" ], "allow": [ "Bash(git commit:*)", "Bash(git add:*)" ] } } Under this policy: The background agent still commits inside its worktree — your review has the diff exactly as the agent produced it. The push at end-of-session fails. The runtime surfaces the failure through agent_completed with pr_url: null. Nothing reaches origin until you git push the branch yourself from the worktree path the notification handed you. This is the pattern the community asked for in #73197, expressed in tools that already exist. It also happens to be the shape the v2.1.221 default is converging on — the runtime just accepts you as the source of authority on which agents can publish.
documents.s: The propose-only pattern that survives every release

documents.t: v2.1.212 and v2.1.221 reshuffled what these three commands do around the auto-PR flow. Read them together: Command What it starts Runs where Auto-PR flow applies? /background New background session Its own row in claude agents Yes /fork (v2.1.212+) Copy of the current conversation into a new background session Its own row in claude agents Yes /subtask (v2.1.221+, was /fork in-session) Ephemeral subagent inside the current session In-conversation No — the parent owns the outcome /resume Reattach to any prior session in claude agents Wherever it was Whatever that session's config was /code-review (v2.1.218+) Review as a background subagent Its own row Yes — but reviews rarely produce PRs, so v2.1.221 usually pushes-without-PR The rename in v2.1.221 (/fork → /subtask for the in-session case) is the important cleanup: /fork now means "hand this conversation to a new background worker and get out of my way," which is the shape the auto-PR flow was designed around. /subtask is what you use when you want a scoped helper in your existing session and don't want the finish-and-publish sequence to fire.

Three real-world details that don't show up in release notes: Background agents count against the concurrency cap. Since v2.1.198, subagents default to background — which means a claude agents list of 25 running sessions will start refusing new spawns with Concurrent subagent limit reached. See Subagent Fleet Limits for the four env vars. The auto-commit is not amend-safe. If two /forks off the same conversation both finish and both push to their own branches, you get two branches, two commits, and (on v2.1.198 – v2.1.220) two PRs. Fine when you meant it as a race; not fine when you thought only one would win. Put a plan step in your agent prompt if you need serialization. A watcher that auto-commits can double-commit. If you also run a repo watcher (a common script that auto-commits changes it sees on disk), it can race the agent's own end-of-session commit — you end up with an empty commit or a merge conflict on push. The safe topology is: the agent owns the worktree, the watcher owns the main clone, and never the twain. Check yourself 0/3 Key takeaways The auto-PR flow lives at the runtime layer, not the settings layer — there is no `backgroundAgents.autoCreatePr` key, and there won't be. Use permissions. v2.1.221 (today's default) always commits and pushes; it opens a draft PR only when the task frames a reviewable change. Read the notification's `pr_url` field to tell which happened. `/fork` now means 'hand this conversation to a background worker'; `/subtask` is what you reach for when you want an in-conversation helper without the finish-and-publish sequence. The propose-only pattern is a permission deny on `Bash(gh pr create:*)`. It survives every version of v2.1.x and every command that produces a background session. Background agents still count against `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`. A fleet of 25 half-finished sessions in `claude agents` will start refusing new spawns.

复制为 Markdown 高级 最后验证时间：2026-06-20。 后台任务、/loop 和调度的确切命令与可用性在不同版本间会变化——请以官方文档为准。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 并非所有事情都是一次快速编辑。Claude Code 能运行超出单次提示寿命的工作：后台的长命令、周期性循环，以及定时运行。
启动一个长时间运行的命令（开发服务器、测试监视器、构建）而不阻塞会话。Claude 继续工作，并在任务产生输出或完成时收到通知。凡是你平常会用 & 放到后台的，都可以用它——但它是受管的，因此 Claude 之后可以读取输出。 不要忙等 在后台启动任务后继续做别的；让完成通知把你带回来，而不是在一个紧密循环里轮询。
/loop 会在一个会话内以周期性间隔运行某个提示或命令——例如"每 5 分钟检查一次部署状态"。给它一个间隔，或让 Claude 自行把控节奏。它非常适合盯着一次 CI 运行，或轮询一个 harness 无法另行通知你的外部作业。
对于那些应当按时钟、持续发生的工作——"每天早上汇总新 issue"、"每小时检查新闻并更新文档"——请使用定时任务 / 例程（cron 风格）。每次运行都从头开始，因此它的指令必须自包含。
需求 使用 运行一个长命令，同时继续工作 后台任务 本次会话内每 N 分钟轮询一次某事 /loop 按计划无限期地做某事 定时例程 自主性需要护栏 任何按计划无人值守执行的操作都应当范围严格、可逆。把它与严格的权限搭配，并阅读加固自主运行。

Mode What runs without asking default Reads only. Shown as Manual acceptEdits Reads, file edits, common filesystem commands plan Reads, plus classifier-approved commands auto Everything, with background safety checks dontAsk Reads and pre-approved tools; the rest is denied bypassPermissions Everything. Isolated containers and VMs only Shift+Tab cycles default, acceptEdits and plan, then bypassPermissions and auto when enabled. Deny rules block in every mode. From v2.1.283 the built-in starting mode for interactive terminal sessions is auto; set permissions.defaultMode to change it. Going deeper: Permissions & Permission Modes.

Aspect Detail Allows Reads, shell commands to explore, a written plan Blocks Edits to your source until you approve the plan Commands Reviewed by the classifier, or prompted when outside the read-only set Not enforced In an interactive terminal session with bypass permissions available Going deeper: Plan Mode.

Event or aspect Detail Configure in hooks in a settings file; /hooks lists them SessionStart A session begins or resumes UserPromptSubmit A prompt is submitted, before processing PreToolUse Before a tool call runs; can block it PostToolUse After a tool call succeeds Stop Claude finishes responding Input Event data as JSON on stdin Exit codes 0: no objection. 2: block the action where the event allows it; stderr is the reason Going deeper: Hooks: Deterministic Automation.

File or syntax What it does ./CLAUDE.md Project instructions, shared through git ./CLAUDE.local.md Personal project notes; add to .gitignore ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md Your preferences, in every project .claude/rules/*.md Topic rules, optionally scoped by paths: @path/to/file Import into CLAUDE.md, up to four hops deep MEMORY.md Auto memory index Claude writes; the first 200 lines or 25KB load Going deeper: CLAUDE.md & Memory Files.

复制为 Markdown 进阶 What you'll learn 理解检查点会记录什么——以及它悄悄不会记录什么 用两种方式打开回溯菜单，并每次都选对恢复操作 区分“恢复”（撤销状态）与“总结”（压缩上下文） 清楚知道检查点为何是 Git 的补充而绝不是替代 最后验证时间：2026-11-02。 检查点的行为、回溯菜单中的操作、快照数量上限和保留时长会随版本变化——请在官方文档中确认。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源.
当你放手让 Claude 去做一项雄心勃勃的大范围改动时，最可怕的问题是“如果做到第三处编辑就出错了怎么办？”检查点（Checkpointing） 就是答案：Claude Code 会在你每次发起一轮对话之前自动为你的代码拍下快照，这样你就可以回溯到任何更早的状态，而不必手动去收拾一个做到一半的重构。 可以把它看作针对整个会话的本地撤销——一张安全网，让你可以放心地说“好，试试那个大胆的方案”。

你不需要创建检查点——它们是自动产生的。 Guided walkthrough1 of 4 1每个开启一轮的提示 = 一个检查点⌄ 每个开启一轮的提示，都会在 Claude 的文件编辑工具运行之前记录下你的代码状态。无需命令，无需配置，没有任何繁琐流程。 ←PreviousNext→ 2只保留最近的 100 个⌄ Claude Code 会为一个会话中最近的 100 个检查点保留文件快照。更早的会被丢弃，因此一个很长的会话无法一路回溯到起点。 ←PreviousNext→ 3它们跨会话持久保留⌄ 检查点与对话一起保存，所以恢复会话之后你仍然可以运行 /rewind，而不只是在当前活跃的会话中。 ←PreviousNext→ 4它们会自我清理⌄ 会话的文件快照会在保留期清理任务中被删除，默认约在该会话最后一次保存快照后的 30 天。回溯到快照已被清除的检查点会失败，并提示“No files were restored”——调高 cleanupPeriodDays 可以让它们保留更久。 ←PreviousNext→

有两种进入方式： Guided walkthrough1 of 2 1运行 /rewind——或它的别名 /checkpoint 和 /undo⌄ 在提示符处输入这个斜杠命令。始终可用。/checkpoint 和 /undo 是同一条命令的别名，想到哪个名字就用哪个。 ←PreviousNext→ 2连按两次 Esc——但仅在输入为空时⌄ 当提示框为空时，连按两次 Esc 会打开回溯菜单。如果框里有文字，连按两次 Esc 则会清除这些文字（被清除的文字会保存到输入历史中，之后按 ↑ 键即可找回）。 ←PreviousNext→ 打开回溯菜单 CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ /rewind Watch out 别名的名字比它的字面意思更亲切：/checkpoint 不会按需拍摄快照（快照是自动的），/undo 也不会自己撤销上一次编辑。三个名字打开的是同一个菜单，你仍然要在其中选择时间点和操作。 菜单会列出本次会话中你发送的每一个提示。选择你想操作的那个时间点，然后选择一个操作。
很多人会在这里搞混。菜单提供两类操作： **恢复（Restore）**操作会改变磁盘上和/或对话中的状态——它们是撤销。 **总结（Summarize）**操作绝不会触碰你的文件——它们把对话压缩以释放上下文窗口空间。 Watch out 恢复 = 撤销（回退代码、对话，或两者）。总结 = 压缩上下文（磁盘上的文件不受影响）。 编辑把东西弄坏了，就用恢复。会话变得臃肿但代码没问题，就用总结。

Guided walkthrough1 of 3 1恢复代码与对话⌄ 把你的文件和聊天历史都回退到所选时间点——干净利落地“回到那一刻”。 ←PreviousNext→ 2恢复对话⌄ 把聊天回退到那条消息，但保留你当前的代码。适合在不丢失想保留的编辑的前提下重新提问。 ←PreviousNext→ 3恢复代码⌄ 回退文件改动但保留对话。撤销编辑，保留关于这些编辑的讨论。 ←PreviousNext→ 两个代码恢复选项只有在所选检查点确实有可回退的已跟踪文件改动时才会出现。如果那个时间点之后没有记录到任何文件编辑，菜单就只提供恢复对话、两个总结选项，以及Never mind（返回消息列表，不做任何更改）。 恢复对话之后（或选择“从此处开始总结”之后），所选消息的原始提示会被放回输入框，方便你重新发送或修改。

两者都会把对话的一部分压缩成 AI 生成的摘要——就像一个有针对性的 /compact，由你选择压缩所选消息的哪一侧。 Guided walkthrough1 of 2 1从此处开始总结⌄ 所选消息之前的消息保持原样。所选消息及其之后的一切都会变成摘要。适合在保留早期上下文完整细节的同时，丢弃一段旁支讨论。 ←PreviousNext→ 2总结到此处为止⌄ 所选消息之前的消息变成摘要；所选消息及其之后的一切保持原样。你仍停留在对话的末尾。适合压缩早期的铺垫闲聊，同时原文保留最近的工作。 ←PreviousNext→ 无论哪种方式，原始消息都仍保留在会话记录中，所以 Claude 仍能参考其中的细节，并且在被压缩的消息原来的位置会出现一个Summarized conversation标记。若想引导摘要的侧重点，用方向键高亮某个总结选项，在显示为add context (optional) 的那一行输入指示，然后按 Enter——如果直接按数字键选择该选项，则会立即总结，不带任何指示。 完整流程请参阅上下文管理——/rewind 的总结操作是手术刀，而 /compact 是大刷子。 What you'll learn 总结会让你留在同一个会话中。如果想另开分支尝试不同的方案、同时保持原会话不变，请改用 /branch 或 claude --continue --fork-session。

如果你在同一个 Claude Code 进程中更早运行过 /clear，回溯菜单的顶部会多出一项：/resume <session-id> (previous session)。选择它即可跳回 /clear 之前的那段对话。 最后验证时间：2026-11-02。 该条目仅在你退出 Claude Code 或恢复另一个会话之前可用。一旦它消失，请改为运行 /resume，并从列表中选择之前的会话。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源.

检查点在失灵之前都显得很神奇。这些缺口很重要： Guided walkthrough1 of 7 1Bash 的改动跟随文件，而不是命令⌄ 跟踪是按文件进行的，只有当 Claude 用它的文件编辑工具编辑过某个文件后，该文件才会进入跟踪。一旦如此，/rewind 也会撤销之后 Bash 命令对同一文件所做的改动——格式化工具或生成器重写一个已被编辑过的文件，是可以回溯的。只有 Bash 碰过的文件不会被跟踪，会保持原样，所以 Claude 从未编辑过、却被 rm 删除的文件需要靠 Git。菜单也反映了这一点：在每个提示下方，它会统计对 Claude 已经编辑过的文件的改动，无论这些改动由什么造成。 ←PreviousNext→ 2大多数子智能体的编辑不会被恢复⌄ 子代理使用同样的文件工具进行编辑，但你的会话通常不会捕获这些编辑。例外是前台的 fork 技能（context: fork 且 background: false），它在你自己的回合中编辑，可以正常回溯。对于任何其他子代理——包括默认的后台 fork 技能，以及后台运行的 /code-review --fix——回溯只会恢复 Claude 在你的对话中已经编辑过的文件；子代理对其他文件的编辑会保留，因此请用 Git 撤销它们。参见 /docs/claude-code/subagents。 ←PreviousNext→ 3外部与并发改动是隐形的⌄ 你在 Claude Code 之外手动做的编辑，以及其他并发会话所做的编辑，通常不会被记录——除非它们恰好触及了当前会话编辑过的那些文件。 ←PreviousNext→ 4会话进行中收到的消息没有检查点⌄ 你在 Claude 工作期间排队发送、并在当前这一轮内送达的消息，会并入这一轮而不是开启新的一轮，所以它自己没有检查点——回溯菜单会把它标记为“No code restore”。要撤销它之后发生的事情，请回溯到开启这一轮的那个提示，这会回溯整整一轮，包括你的消息到达之前已完成的工作。直接选中这条被标记的消息，仍然可以使用“恢复对话”，你的文件保持原样。 ←PreviousNext→ 5对话恢复要到你发送下一条提示后才会保存⌄ Claude Code 会把回退后的对话与你发送的下一条提示一起保存——所以如果你在发送之前退出，恢复会话时被回退的消息会重新出现。退出前先给 Claude 发一条提示，恢复才会生效；如果之后想再次去掉回来的消息，运行 /rewind，选择同一条提示，然后选择 Restore conversation。无论哪种情况，你恢复的文件都保持回退后的状态，所以受影响的只有对话。 ←PreviousNext→ 6符号链接和硬链接会被跳过⌄ 恢复时会跳过任何属于符号链接或硬链接的已跟踪路径，并警告“Restored the code, but skipped N files”；这些文件保持当前内容。dotfile 管理器的符号链接和 pnpm 的硬链接都会碰到这个问题。恢复之前先运行 /debug，调试日志里就会列出被跳过的路径。 ←PreviousNext→ 7它是会话级别的，而非历史⌄ 检查点是快速的本地恢复手段。它们不是提交，不是分支，也无法与团队共享。 ←PreviousNext→

documents.t: 它们解决的是不同的问题，所以要搭配使用。 检查点（/rewind） Git 范围 一个会话 整个项目历史 粒度 每个开启一轮的提示，自动 每次提交，刻意为之 跟踪 bash 造成的改动？ 仅限 Claude 已编辑过的文件 是（一旦暂存/提交） 寿命 最近 100 个检查点，会话结束后约 30 天清理 永久 可共享 / 可协作 否 是 心智模型 “本地撤销” “永久历史” Pro tip 在冒险的大范围运行之前，先用 Git 提交可工作的状态——那是你持久的底线。 用 /rewind 在两次提交之间快速进行会话内恢复，而不会弄脏你的 Git 历史。 对于 Claude 从不直接编辑的文件——只有破坏性的 bash（rm/mv）或后台子代理才会碰的那些——请依靠 Git。只有当 Claude 用自己的文件工具编辑过某个文件后，rewind 才会覆盖它。

documents.t: Guided walkthrough1 of 4 1探索备选方案⌄ 尝试一个大胆的实现，如果不喜欢，就把代码和对话恢复到分叉点，再试另一条路。 ←PreviousNext→ 2从糟糕的编辑中恢复⌄ 三个提示之前的一次编辑引入了 bug？把代码恢复到它之前，而不是去调试那堆残局。 ←PreviousNext→ 3迭代某个功能⌄ 尝试各种变体，始终知道一个已知良好的状态只需一次 /rewind 就能回到。 ←PreviousNext→ 4释放上下文空间⌄ 一次冗长的调试岔路耗尽了你的上下文窗口？从中点开始往后总结，同时完整保留你最初的指示。 ←PreviousNext→ 自测一下 0/3 Key takeaways 检查点是在每个开启一轮的提示之前自动拍下的快照——会话的本地撤销。保留最近 100 个，会话结束后约 30 天清理。 用 /rewind（别名：/checkpoint、/undo）或在输入为空时连按两次 Esc 打开回溯菜单；它会列出你发送的每一个提示。 恢复操作撤销状态（代码、对话，或两者）；总结操作压缩上下文，绝不触碰文件。 跟踪是按文件进行的，从 Claude 用文件工具编辑它时开始——此后，即使是对该文件的 Bash 改动也会被回溯。Claude 从未编辑过的文件（仅 bash、外部、并发、大多数子代理改动）不会被跟踪，符号链接或硬链接路径在 restore 时会被跳过。 检查点是 Git 的补充，而不是替代：想想“本地撤销”与“永久、可共享的历史”。

复制为 Markdown 入门 最后验证时间：2026-10-06。 文件位置、加载顺序和导入语法均来自官方记忆文档（「Claude 如何记住你的项目」），该文档现在描述了两种机制：由你编写的 CLAUDE.md 文件，以及 Claude 自己编写的自动记忆。导入最多解析到四跳深度。具体细节请在那里确认——这些细节会变化。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 如果你只做一件事来让 Claude Code 变得更好，那就做这件。CLAUDE.md 是一个纯文本文件，Claude 会在每次会话开始时读取它——它是你项目的常驻简报。 What you'll learn 为什么 CLAUDE.md 是收益最高的单一 Claude Code 设置 记忆层级如何加载，从托管策略一直到 CLAUDE.local.md 自动记忆与你自己编写的 CLAUDE.md 有何不同 如何用 /init 生成一份起始文件并精简它 什么内容应该写进 CLAUDE.md——以及什么应该排除在外 @imports 如何让你引用文档而无需重复其内容
没有它，你每次会话都要重新解释你的项目（「我们用 pnpm，测试在 __tests__ 里，别碰 /generated……」）。有了它，Claude 早已知晓。这里写好的指令会一次性改善未来每一次交互。

documents.t: Claude Code 会从多个位置加载记忆，并按加载顺序合并它们，作用域最宽泛的在前——因此项目指令会在用户指令之后进入上下文： 托管策略——由你的 IT/DevOps 团队分发的组织级指令。路径因操作系统而异：macOS 上是 /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md，Linux 和 WSL 上是 /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md，Windows 上是 C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md。 用户指令（~/.claude/CLAUDE.md）——你在所有项目中的个人偏好。 项目指令（./CLAUDE.md 或 ./.claude/CLAUDE.md，已提交）——这个仓库如何运作。与团队共享。如果你的仓库使用 AGENTS.md，它可以代替这些文件加载，也可以与它们一起加载。 本地指令（./CLAUDE.local.md）——只属于你自己的项目专属笔记，比如一个沙箱 URL。把它加进 .gitignore。 位于你工作目录之上的目录层级中的文件会在启动时加载；而子目录中的文件按需加载——当 Claude 接触到那个区域里的东西时才加载。 Pro tip 一个文件已经不够用了？把指令拆分到 .claude/rules/*.md——每个文件一个主题，会被递归发现。没有 paths frontmatter 的规则会在启动时加载，优先级与 .claude/CLAUDE.md 相同；加上 paths frontmatter 之后，规则只在 Claude 处理匹配的文件时才加载，这能节省上下文。

CLAUDE.md 是记忆中由你编写的那一半。Claude Code 还会保留自动记忆——Claude 从你的纠正和偏好中自己写下的笔记，按仓库存储，并在每次会话中与你的 CLAUDE.md 文件一起加载。 CLAUDE.md 文件 自动记忆 谁来编写 你 Claude 包含什么 指令和规则 学到的经验和模式 作用范围 项目、用户或组织 按仓库，跨 worktree 共享 两者都是上下文，而不是强制约束：Claude 把它们当作可以权衡的指引，而不是必须服从的配置。如果要无论 Claude 怎么决定都硬性拦截某个操作，请改用 PreToolUse 钩子。 Watch out 自动记忆只会加载它的前 200 行或 25 KB——一个臃肿的 MEMORY.md 会被静默截断。完整的启动开销拆解见上下文预算审计。

Guided walkthrough1 of 3 1在项目里运行 /init⌄ Claude 会检查代码并自动为你起草一份 CLAUDE.md。 ←PreviousNext→ 2把它精简下来⌄ 草稿只是起点，而非终点。把它修剪成真实且有用的内容。 ←PreviousNext→ 3借用一个模板⌄ 从 CLAUDE.md 模板页面取一份现成的起始模板，并按你的仓库进行调整。 ←PreviousNext→ 生成一份 CLAUDE.md 草稿 CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ /init 从 CLAUDE.md 模板里取一份现成的起始模板。
用两句话说明项目是什么。 技术栈，以及如何运行 / 测试 / lint。 Claude 推断不出来的约定（命名、结构、提交风格）。 护栏：「声明完成前先跑测试」、「绝不编辑 /vendor」、「绝不提交密钥」。
Watch out Claude 会字面地遵循 CLAUDE.md——过时、含糊或一厢情愿的指令反而有害。 描述项目当下实际的运作方式；简短且真实，胜过冗长且理想化。 避免粘贴巨大的文档（改用 @imports），避免密钥，避免你实际并不遵循的规则。 定期复查它，让它随项目演进而保持准确。

引入已有文档而不是复制它们——例如用 @path/to/file 导入引用你的风格指南，这样就只有一个权威来源。相对路径和绝对路径都可以；相对路径是相对于包含该导入的那个文件解析的，而不是相对于你的工作目录。被导入的文件还可以再导入其他文件，最多到四跳深度。 在被坑到之前，有两个语法陷阱值得先知道： 空格需要反斜杠。 @Design\ Docs/api-conventions.md 可以工作；没有反斜杠的话，路径会在第一个空格处截断。而用引号把它包起来则完全不会导入该文件。 反引号表示退出解析。 导入解析会跳过代码片段和围栏代码块，所以 `@README` 仍然是字面文本，而单独写 @README 则会导入该文件。你就是这样在提到一个路径时不去加载它。 完整参考见官方记忆文档。 Pro tip 单一权威来源：用 @imports 引用文件，而不是把它的内容粘贴进 CLAUDE.md。 如果文档已经存在，链接它——别复制它。副本会逐渐过时。

自测一下 0/6 Key takeaways CLAUDE.md 是收益最高的设置：它会一次性改善未来每一次会话。 记忆按最宽泛优先加载：先是托管策略，然后是用户（~/.claude/CLAUDE.md）、项目（./CLAUDE.md 或 ./.claude/CLAUDE.md），最后是本地（./CLAUDE.local.md）。子目录中的文件按需加载。 自动记忆是另一半——Claude 自己的笔记，按仓库存储，每次会话都会加载。两者都是上下文，而不是强制约束：要硬性拦截某件事，请用钩子。 一个文件已经不够用了？把它拆分到 .claude/rules/*.md，并用 paths frontmatter 限定规则的适用范围。 从 /init 开始，然后把草稿精简成真正真实的内容。 保持简短且真实——大型文档用 @imports（最多四跳），并且绝不提交密钥。
AGENTS.md 与跨工具互操作——让每个编码代理共享同一份指令文件 规划模式——安全的首次改动 权限与模式——Claude 可以无人值守做哪些事 实战演练：为真实仓库定制 Claude Code 分享此页面 X LinkedIn Reddit Hacker News 复制链接

复制为 Markdown 进阶 最后验证时间：2026-10-07。 下文的所有命令、标志、默认值和版本下限均来自官方 CLI 参考，阅读日期为 2026-10-07。标志会在不同版本之间出现和变化，而且参考文档明确指出 claude --help 并未列出所有标志——因此 --help 里没有的标志，不一定在你的构建里不存在。请以参考文档为准，而不是帮助文本，并用 claude -v 检查你的版本。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 大多数人只学会命令行的三样东西——claude、claude -c 和 claude -p——然后就停下了。如果你只是坐在它面前使用，停在这里完全合理。可一旦你把 Claude Code 放进脚本、CI 任务、后台队列或同事手里，这些标志就不再只是便利，而是决定一次运行花一美元还是卡住一小时的关键。 本页不是参考表格的第二份拷贝。它讲的是学习这套界面的顺序、真正会改变结果的标志，以及让人实实在在浪费过时间的四个陷阱。 What you'll learn 你可以启动的六种会话，以及哪个标志选择哪一种 让无人值守运行有边界、可应答、可解析的五标志约定 为什么修改 --append-system-prompt 后再运行 --continue 看起来毫无作用——已记录提示词规则 --bare、--safe-mode 和 --restricted 有何区别，何时该用哪个 从 shell 驱动后台会话：agents、attach、logs、respawn、rm、daemon 人们容易混淆的标志对：--tools、--allowedTools 与 --disallowedTools

documents.t: 其他所有决定都由此而来。Claude Code 可以启动六种本质不同的东西，而选择其中一种的标志，通常是你最先输入的内容。 你想要 标志 你得到 一场你全程观看的对话 （无） 在当前终端中的交互式会话 一个答案，然后退出 -p / --print 非交互式运行，输出到 stdout 能在当前终端关闭后继续的工作 --bg / --background 一个后台会话；打印其 ID 以及如何管理它 一个隔离的分支用来试验 -w / --worktree 位于 <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name> 的 git worktree 在 Anthropic 的机器上工作 --cloud 一个云会话，或排入现有云会话的后续任务 用手机驱动当前会话 --rc / --remote-control 一个同时可从 claude.ai 或 Claude 应用控制的交互式会话 其中两个不能组合：--bg 和 -p 互斥，因为一个立即返回，另一个要等待答案。如果你想在后台运行的是 shell 命令而不是 Claude 会话，请将 --bg 与 --exec 搭配使用： Run the test suite as a background job, not a Claude session CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ claude --bg --exec 'pytest -x' 另外，--bg 在启动前会检查该目录的工作区信任状态——因此在不受信任的仓库里启动后台会话，会在一开始就失败，而不是做到一半才失败。

documents.t: 这是本页价值最高的内容。无人值守的 claude -p 运行有三种出错方式，是交互式会话根本不会遇到的：它可能在没人应答的权限提示上停滞，可能循环得远超你的预期，也可能在你的脚本需要数据时输出散文。五个标志把这三种情况都堵住了。 Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1以非交互方式运行 — -p⌄ `claude -p "query"` 打印答案后退出。下面的一切都只适用于 print 模式，所以这个标志是其余各项的入口。 ←PreviousNext→ 2决定谁来应答权限提示 — --permission-prompts⌄ 默认值是 `host`，它会把提示发送给 Agent SDK 宿主或 `--permission-prompt-tool`。当没有人能应答时（比如 cron 任务或 CI 步骤），传入 `--permission-prompts none`：运行不再咨询或等待宿主，任何会弹出提示的操作都会被拒绝，除非有 `PermissionRequest` 钩子允许，并且会告知 Claude 不要重试。完全没有宿主的 `-p` 运行本来就会拒绝这些请求；此时该标志主要是阻止重试。需要 v2.1.259 或更高版本。再搭配范围狭窄的 `--allowedTools` 规则，让拒绝成为少数情况而不是常态。 ←PreviousNext→ 3为循环设界 — --max-turns⌄ 默认没有轮数限制。`--max-turns 3` 在达到上限时以错误退出。把它当作防止失控代理循环的绊线，而不是预算。 ←PreviousNext→ 4为开销设界 — --max-budget-usd⌄ `--max-budget-usd 5.00` 会在客户端成本估算达到上限时停止。子代理的花费计入其中；一旦达到上限，再启动子代理会失败并提示 `Budget limit reached`，正在运行的后台子代理也会被停止。上限的强制执行需要 v2.1.217 或更高版本。 ←PreviousNext→ 5让输出可解析 — --output-format 或 --json-schema⌄ `--output-format json` 给你一个结构化的外层包装。`--json-schema '<schema>'` 更进一步：Claude Code 会依据你的 JSON Schema 校验最终答案，并在 schema 无效时提前报错，所以你的脚本再也不用对散文写正则了。 ←PreviousNext→ A CI step that cannot hang, cannot loop forever, and cannot overspend CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ claude -p "Review the staged diff and list bugs" \ --permission-prompts none \ --allowedTools "Read" "Bash(git diff *)" \ --max-turns 6 \ --max-budget-usd 2.00 \ --output-format json --max-budget-usd 是估算，不是你的账单 Claude Code 是用它自己的客户端成本估算来对照上限的，这可能与你实际被计费的金额不同。 当你用 --continue 或 --resume 回到一段对话时，从先前运行恢复的总额不计入上限——所以在 2 美元上限下连续三次恢复运行，总花费可能超过 2 美元。 把它当作单次运行的断路器。如果需要对整个账户或项目设置真正的上限，请参阅 Hard Spend Caps。 关于在没有人在场的情况下放手让运行继续的完整做法——允许什么、屏蔽什么、记录什么——请参阅加固自主运行和无头模式与 Agent SDK。关于服务商层面的上限，请参阅 Hard Spend Caps。

documents.t: 有五个标志影响系统提示词。四个设置其文本；第五个决定对话是否保留它起初所用的文本。 标志 作用 --system-prompt 用你的文本替换整个默认提示词 --system-prompt-file 用某个文件的内容替换它 --append-system-prompt 把你的文本追加到默认提示词后 --append-system-prompt-file 把某个文件的内容追加到默认提示词后 --system-prompt-snapshot off 在每次请求时重建提示词；on（默认）复用已记录的那一份 在追加与替换之间做选择，是在选择身份。追加会保留 Claude Code 默认的工具指引、安全说明和编码约定，并把你的规则叠加其上——适合每次运行的指令、输出格式或项目上下文。替换则会丢弃所有这些，包括工具指引，所以只有当这个场景确实不是编码助手时才适合：比如无人看管的流水线里的非编码代理。一旦替换，任务仍然需要的一切都由你负责。 你可以组合使用。把追加标志和替换标志一起传入，会先替换默认提示词，再追加你的文本。从 v2.1.283 起，你还可以把一个标志与它自己的文件形式一起传入——--append-system-prompt 以及 --append-system-prompt-file——Claude Code 会同时使用两者，无论你以什么顺序输入，文件内容都排在前面。 陷阱：恢复的对话会沿用它诞生时的提示词 Claude Code 在一段对话的第一次请求时构建一次系统提示词，并把它记录在会话中。 在对话被压缩之前，之后的每次请求都使用这份已记录的提示词——包括 --resume 或 --continue 之后。 所以你编辑了 --append-system-prompt 的文本，重新运行 claude --continue，却什么都没变。标志没有坏；只是这段对话仍在使用那份记录。 新文本会在对话压缩之后，或在全新的对话中生效。 若要在多次 --continue 运行之间迭代措辞，请传入 --system-prompt-snapshot off，这样每次请求都会重建提示词。需要 v2.1.257 或更高版本。 在混合了稳定指令与每次运行上下文的替换提示词中，还有一个值得了解的技巧。在两者之间放一行只含 __SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY__ 的内容：Claude Code 会在第一个这样的行处切分并将其移除，因此上半部分保持缓存，下半部分则随运行变化。需要 v2.1.275 或更高版本。这为何会影响你的账单，见 Prompt Caching。 对于多用户的脚本化工作负载，--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections 会把每个用户的上下文（比如自动记忆的位置）从系统提示词移到第一条用户消息中——这样不同机器上的同一任务可以共享同一个缓存前缀。它只作用于默认提示词，当你设置 --system-prompt 或 --system-prompt-file 时会被忽略。

documents.t: 人们会混用它们，然后纳闷症状为什么没变。它们解决的是三个不同的问题。 --bare --safe-mode --restricted 它解决的问题 启动对脚本化调用来说太慢 我的配置坏了，却不知道是哪一部分 评测框架不得触碰这台共享机器 CLAUDE.md、技能、命令、子代理、插件、MCP、自动记忆 不会被发现 不会被加载 只加载托管设置和 --settings 内置工具 Bash、文件读取、文件编辑 正常工作 运行命令/代码的工具和 WebFetch 会被移除，除非在 --tools 中逐个点名 文件访问 正常 正常 限制在工作目录内 bypassPermissions 允许 允许 拒绝 托管策略 生效 仍然生效，包括策略钩子和状态栏 生效 副作用 设置 CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE 设置 CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE 拒绝创建云会话 把这张表读作意图的递进：--bare 关乎速度，--safe-mode 关乎诊断，--restricted 关乎隔离。一个有用的细节：通过 --add-dir 传入的目录里的技能，在 --bare 下仍会加载，这就是在其余全被剥离的运行中恰好保留一项能力的办法。 当某处出了问题而你分不清是 Claude Code 还是你自己的配置时，--safe-mode 是首选——包括你想弄清是否某个自定义项触发了自动模型回退的时候。把它与 claude doctor 搭配使用，后者无需启动会话就会打印只读的安装与设置诊断信息。（会话内的 /doctor 命令是另一回事：它还可以应用修复。）更多从症状出发的排查见排查 Claude Code 问题。--restricted 需要 v2.1.248 或更高版本。

documents.t: 一旦你用 --bg 启动会话，终端就成了控制面板。整个生命周期都有对应的命令，而且都不需要打开交互式界面。 Guided walkthrough1 of 6 1查看正在运行什么 — claude agents⌄ 打开代理视图，用于监控和调度并行的后台会话。用于脚本时，`--json` 以 JSON 数组形式打印活动会话，`--json --all` 还包括已完成的会话。`--cwd <path>` 将范围缩小到在该目录下启动的会话。打开视图本身需要交互式终端；JSON 形式则不需要。 ←PreviousNext→ 2查看某一个的内部 — claude logs⌄ `claude logs <id|name>` 打印后台会话最近的输出。从 v2.1.290 起，你可以传入某个运行中会话名称的一部分来代替 ID——所以 `claude logs auth` 通常就够了。 ←PreviousNext→ 3接管它 — claude attach⌄ `claude attach <id|name>` 把一个后台会话带到当前终端。部分名称匹配同样需要 v2.1.290 或更高版本。 ←PreviousNext→ 4重启它 — claude respawn⌄ `claude respawn <id>` 重启一个会话（无论运行中还是已停止），对话保持完整。`--all` 重启所有运行中的会话——升级 Claude Code 二进制文件之后该做的操作。 ←PreviousNext→ 5停止并清理 — claude stop、claude rm⌄ `claude stop <id>`（也可用 `claude kill`）停止一个会话。`claude rm <id>` 把它从列表中移除；转录内容仍保留在你的机器上，仍可通过 `claude --resume` 访问。如果因该会话的 worktree 而拒绝移除，拒绝信息会打印出接下来该传入的确切标志——`--discard-unpushed`（v2.1.260+）或 `--force-remove-worktree`（v2.1.268+）。 ←PreviousNext→ 6当整个系统卡住时 — claude daemon⌄ 后台会话由一个监督进程托管。`claude daemon status` 打印其状态、版本、套接字目录和 worker 数量，并在其未运行时以 1 退出。`claude daemon logs` 跟踪 `~/.claude/daemon.log`。`claude daemon stop --any --keep-workers` 重启监督进程，同时让会话保持存活，等下一个监督进程来重新连接。 ←PreviousNext→ 与此相对、从会话内部看的另一面——工作如何转入后台，以及转入后会保留什么——见后台任务、/loop 与调度。

documents.t: 值得预先澄清的六个混淆 --tools 限制存在哪些内置工具。--allowedTools 指定哪些调用可跳过权限提示。--disallowedTools 拒绝调用。这是三件不同的事，传错一个是“为什么它还在问我”最常见的原因。 --tools 完全不影响 MCP 工具。若要把它们也移除，请加上 --disallowedTools "mcp__*"。 --disallowedTools 中的裸名称会把该工具从 Claude 的上下文中移除；而像 Bash(rm *) 这样带范围的规则会让工具保持可用，只拒绝匹配的调用。 --dangerously-skip-permissions 会在 bypassPermissions 模式下启动。--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions 只是把该模式加入 Shift+Tab 循环，这样你可以先在 plan 模式启动，之后再切换。你真正想要的几乎总是第二个。 --add-dir 授予文件访问权限，但 Claude Code 不会从这些目录中发现大部分 .claude/ 配置。添加一个目录并不等于采纳它的配置。 --desktop 不接受提示词，也不接受除 --verbose 和 --debug 系列之外的其他标志，因为桌面应用会自己启动会话。需要 v2.1.285 或更高版本。 还有一个小小的体验细节：如果你把子命令敲错，Claude Code 会给出最接近的匹配建议并退出，而不会启动会话——claude udpate 会打印 Did you mean claude update?，而不是打开一段你并不想要的对话。

documents.t: Check yourself 0/3 Key takeaways 先选会话类型——决定类型的那个标志会约束你之后能传的所有其他标志。 无人值守运行需要五个标志，而不是一个：-p、--permission-prompts none、--max-turns、--max-budget-usd，以及结构化的输出格式。 把 --max-budget-usd 当作单次运行的断路器，而不是账单上限。它是客户端估算，恢复的总额会漏过它。 对话在第一次请求时记录其系统提示词。如果提示词的修改似乎被忽略，原因就在于此——迭代时使用 --system-prompt-snapshot off。 --bare 是速度，--safe-mode 是诊断，--restricted 是隔离。选错一个会浪费一个下午。 --help 在设计上就不完整。CLI 参考才是事实来源，版本下限也很重要——在怪罪某个标志之前，先检查 claude -v。
