复制为 Markdown 进阶 What you'll learn Trace the real escalation path — automated classifier, specialised review queue, trained human reviewer, account ban, law-enforcement referral — and see where the latency actually sits (days, not seconds) Learn the asymmetry OpenAI published and almost nobody quotes: threats to others may be referred to police, self-harm cases explicitly are not Do the retention arithmetic across providers, including the two numbers that survive every privacy control you can toggle Understand why a zero-data-retention contract does not exempt you from the safety pipeline — and why Anthropic's most capable models cannot be used under ZDR at all See what incognito, temporary and activity-off modes actually govern (training and history) versus what they do not (abuse monitoring) Decide, per class of text, which surface it belongs on — and what to do instead when the honest answer is 'none of them' Between August and early October 2026, three conversations with a commercial AI assistant publicly became police matters. One produced a felony arrest. The pattern is not a glitch and it is not new policy — it is the documented operation of an abuse pipeline every major provider runs, described in help-centre articles that almost nobody reads before pasting. The useful question is not "do they read my chats?" — the answer has been yes, in a narrow and specific sense, for years. The useful questions are what triggers a human to look, what a human is authorised to do next, and which of your privacy settings touch that path at all. The third answer is the one that surprises people: mostly none of them.
documents.s: Who Reads Your AI Chats — Safety Review, Police Referral, and the Retention You Can't Delete

documents.t: 最后验证时间：2026-10-06。 Case facts are from contemporaneous reporting and are the subject of pending criminal proceedings; charges are allegations, not findings. Policy figures are from provider documentation current on the verify date and change without notice — re-read the linked help-centre articles before relying on any number here. 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. San Francisco, August 2026. A Claude user allegedly wrote that he had bought an AR-15 and had Anthropic's CEO "in his sights." Per the police report cited by The San Francisco Standard, the messages were sent on Friday 14 August at 2:30 p.m. Anthropic notified SFPD the following Tuesday at 9 a.m. Officers attended Anthropic's office; the subject was not present and, as of that reporting, had not been arrested or charged. He told the Standard he had not been serious. Anthropic's statement: the account was banned and the case referred, and "this is our safeguards process working as intended." Florida, late September 2026. Carli Michelle Heller of Bonita Springs had been using Claude much as one uses a journal. According to the arrest report, on 26 September she wrote that she would shoot up the Lee County Sheriff's Office, and on 27 September that she had obtained a new gun. Automated systems flagged the text, a human review team assessed it, Anthropic reported it, deputies located her at home and detained her without incident. She was charged with making a written threat of violence — a second-degree felony — with a court date in November. Tom's Hardware counted the Florida case as at least the third Claude conversation to reach police since August.
documents.s: What actually happened in the three cases

documents.t: The latency is days, not seconds. Friday afternoon to Tuesday morning is roughly four days. This is a review queue staffed by people, not a tripwire wired to a dispatcher. That cuts both ways: it is not real-time surveillance, and it is also not a system that can intervene in a genuinely imminent event. A human made the call. In both cases the automated classifier only routed. The decision to contact police was made by a trained reviewer reading the text. The thing people find most uncomfortable — an employee read my private journal — is the deliberate design, not the failure mode. Account termination came first. Banning preceded or accompanied referral. If you are ever on the wrong side of a classifier for innocent reasons, the first symptom is losing access, not a phone call.

Every major provider runs some version of this. The vocabulary differs; the shape does not. Guided walkthrough1 of 5 11 — Automated classification on every request⌄ Safety classifiers score inputs and outputs. This runs on essentially all traffic to consumer surfaces and is not something you can opt out of; it is how usage policies are enforced at scale. Scores are data in their own right, and they are retained separately from the conversation — a distinction that matters enormously later on this page. ←PreviousNext→ 22 — Routing to a specialised queue⌄ High-scoring conversations in specific categories are routed out of the normal flow. OpenAI's published description: 'When we detect users who are planning to harm others, we route their conversations to specialized pipelines where they are reviewed by a small team trained on our usage policies and who are authorized to take action, including banning accounts.' Anthropic's Usage Policy states that its Safeguards Team 'will implement detection and monitoring to enforce our Usage Policy.' ←PreviousNext→ 33 — Human review⌄ A trained reviewer reads the conversation. At Google this function is explicit and broader than abuse: a subset of Gemini chats are reviewed by humans, including trained service providers, to assess quality and safety and to address Terms of Service violations. Google's own instruction to users is blunt: do not enter confidential information you would not want a reviewer to see. ←PreviousNext→ 44 — Enforcement⌄ Throttling, suspension or termination. Anthropic's Usage Policy reserves exactly this: 'we may throttle, suspend, or terminate your access to our products or services.' This is the overwhelmingly common outcome and the only one most flagged users ever experience. ←PreviousNext→ 55 — External referral, in a narrow band⌄ Two distinct triggers. Mandatory: Anthropic states that when it detects CSAM, including AI-generated CSAM, or the coercion or enticement of a minor, it will report to the relevant authorities. Discretionary: OpenAI's position is that 'if human reviewers determine that a case involves an imminent threat of serious physical harm to others, we may refer it to law enforcement.' Anthropic's Privacy Policy grounds the same discretion in a good-faith belief that disclosure is reasonably necessary to, among other things, 'prevent serious harm to any person or to property.' ←PreviousNext→

When OpenAI published the passage above, the sentence that followed it got far less attention and is arguably more consequential: OpenAI stated it is "currently not referring self-harm cases to law enforcement to respect people's privacy given the uniquely private nature of ChatGPT interactions." So the published line is drawn at harm to others, not at distress. Someone in crisis about themselves is handled inside the product — crisis resources, model behaviour changes, possibly human review — without a police referral. Someone who writes a threat against a third party is in a different pipeline entirely. If you only remember one thing about escalation thresholds, remember that the line is about who gets hurt, and that it is a policy choice a provider can revise.

This is the section that changes behaviour, because the numbers are longer than almost anyone assumes and several of them are immune to the controls in your settings panel. What Provider Duration Survives you deleting it? Normal conversation you delete Anthropic (consumer) Gone from history immediately, purged from back-end storage within 30 days — Conversation flagged as violating the Usage Policy Anthropic Inputs and outputs up to 2 years Yes Trust-and-safety classification scores for that conversation Anthropic Up to 7 years Yes Data you opted into model improvement Anthropic (consumer) De-identified, up to 5 years in training pipelines Per opt-out at the time Chat read by a human reviewer Google (Gemini Apps) Up to 3 years, disconnected from your Google Account Yes — deleting your activity does not remove it Gemini Apps Activity on Google Auto-delete at 18 months by default (adjustable to 3 or 36 months, or off) — Gemini Apps Activity off Google Temporary chats kept 72 hours to respond to you and protect safety — ChatGPT Temporary Chat OpenAI Not in history, not in memory, not used for training; may be retained up to 30 days for safety — Prompts and completions on a Covered Model Anthropic At least 30 days, mandatory, then auto-deleted — Two rows deserve to be read twice. Seven years of classification scores. The conversation itself may be gone; the structured judgement about it persists for the better part of a decade. A classification score is not a copy of your text, but it is a durable, account-linked assertion that your text scored a certain way on a certain category. For anyone reasoning about long-term exposure, that is the real retention horizon, and it is roughly 85× longer than the 30-day purge window people cite when they say deletion works. Three years that outlive deletion. Google is explicit that human-reviewed chats and their associated metadata — language, device type, location information, feedback — are not deleted when you delete your activity, precisely because they have been disconnected from your account. Anonymisation is what makes the retention defensible and also what makes it permanent from your side: there is no longer an account handle to issue the delete against. Google tries to disconnect reviewed chats before a human sees them, but anything you typed into the message is part of the message.

This is the single most common misconception among developers who believe they have solved the problem contractually. Zero Data Retention for Claude Code on Claude for Enterprise means prompts and responses are processed in real time and "not stored by Anthropic after the response is returned" — "except where needed to comply with law or combat misuse." Anthropic's own documentation spells the exception out: Even with ZDR enabled, Anthropic may retain data where required by law or to address Usage Policy violations. If a session is flagged for a policy violation, Anthropic may retain the associated inputs and outputs for up to 2 years. And separately, on what ZDR never covered in the first place: Anthropic still retains User Safety classifier results in order to enforce our Usage Policy. So the correct mental model is: ZDR removes the storage, not the pipeline. Classification still happens on every request; the scores are still kept; a flagged session still gets a two-year retention. ZDR is an excellent control against routine retention and a poor one against abuse-response retention, which is exactly the retention that matters if something you sent is ever contested.

Anthropic documents these explicitly, and each has bitten someone: It does not cover the web app or Cowork. ZDR for Claude Code covers Claude Code inference. Chat on claude.ai through the same Enterprise interface, and Cowork sessions, follow standard retention. It does not follow the user, only the organisation. ZDR applies to requests that authenticate into a ZDR-enabled org. A developer who signs in with a personal account, or with an API key from a different org, is simply not covered. Anthropic's answer is the forceLoginMethod and forceLoginOrgUUID managed settings — worth deploying if you believe ZDR is load-bearing for you. It does not propagate to new organisations. ZDR is enabled per-org by Anthropic's account team and does not automatically apply to new orgs created under the same account. It does not cover third parties. Data processed by MCP servers and external integrations is outside ZDR entirely. (See What Your Agent Uploads and Securing MCP Servers.)
documents.s: Four more things ZDR does not do

documents.t: Anthropic designates its most capable models — currently Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5 and Claude Fable 5 — as Covered Models, which require data retention by default. Prompts and completions are retained for at least 30 days, then automatically deleted, and the retained window is assessed by automated safety systems designed to flag harmful content. The stated reason is the genuinely interesting part, because it is an admission about the limits of per-request filtering: Because "some forms of misuse only become detectable across many requests, these models require safeguards that operate over a retained window of usage data rather than on a single request at a time." A single request that assembles one benign-looking piece of a dangerous whole is invisible to a stateless classifier. Detecting the pattern requires remembering the requests. That is a real security argument, and it means capability and retention are now coupled by design: for these models, you can have the frontier capability or you can have zero retention, not both. ZDR is unavailable for Covered Models in standard configurations; where an org or workspace lacks the mandatory retention, requests for those models are rejected server-side regardless of client configuration, and Claude Code's best alias quietly resolves to Opus instead of Fable. Anthropic has signalled an Enterprise Frontier Safeguards path for eligible customers to use Fable 5 and 5.1 under ZDR for internal business applications, rolling out in autumn 2026 — confirm current status with your account team rather than assuming either way. For the model-side view of this, see the Fable 5.1 Field Guide, which notes the same mandatory 30-day window from the API-behaviour angle: a request from an org without it returns a 400.
documents.s: Covered Models: the capability/retention trade is now explicit

documents.t: Here is the clean separation, and it is the practical thesis of this page. Control Governs Does not govern Anthropic incognito chat Excluded from model improvement even when improvement is on Safety flagging and the retention that follows it ChatGPT Temporary Chat History, memory, training Safety/abuse retention — up to 30 days per OpenAI's FAQ Gemini Apps Activity off Training, human review of future chats, long-term activity storage A 72-hour window kept to respond to you and protect safety Delete conversation Your history, and back-end copies on a purge timer Flagged content, classification scores, already-reviewed chats Zero Data Retention Routine storage of prompts and completions Classification itself, score retention, flagged-session retention Read the right-hand column as a single sentence: consumer privacy controls are training-and-history controls. None of them is an abuse-monitoring control. That is not a gotcha hidden in fine print — it is the only way a usage policy can be enforceable at all. But it does mean the mental model "incognito means nobody sees this" is wrong in a way that matters. One control genuinely does narrow human review: Google lets you turn off the pathway that feeds chats to reviewers, via myaccount.google.com → Data and Privacy → Gemini Apps Activity → Turn off. Future conversations are then not sent for human review and not used for training. Chats already reviewed are still inside their three-year window.
documents.s: What your privacy settings actually control

documents.t: Heller was charged under Florida's written-threats statute, Fla. Stat. 836.10. Its elements are worth reading because they explain how writing to a chatbot can be charged at all. The statute reaches a person who sends, posts or transmits — or procures the sending, posting or transmission of — a writing or other record, including an electronic record, "in any manner in which it may be viewed by another person," containing a threat to kill or do bodily harm, or to conduct a mass shooting or an act of terrorism. It is a second-degree felony. Two observations, offered as reading of the statutory text rather than as legal advice: The text does not require an intended human recipient. It requires a record transmitted in a manner in which it may be viewed by another person. A conversation stored on a provider's servers and readable by that provider's reviewers is not obviously outside that language. This is precisely the gap between what a user feels they are doing (writing privately) and what the statute describes (transmitting a viewable electronic record). Intent is still an element. Florida pattern elements require that the defendant intended the threat as a true threat — the doctrinal line that separates a prosecutable threat from hyperbole or venting, and the obvious terrain for a defence. "I was just venting to a chatbot" is a factual argument about intent, not a safe harbour created by the medium. If you need the statute itself, it is published by the Florida Senate; the link is in the sources. If you are in actual legal trouble, talk to a lawyer, not a field guide.

The honest decision procedure, by class of text. Class of text Right surface Why Ordinary work, code, writing Any hosted assistant The pipeline exists but is irrelevant to you Confidential business data Commercial/Enterprise tier with the right terms; ZDR if you qualify Routine retention removed; abuse retention remains Regulated data (health, financial) BAA/HIPAA-configured enterprise deployment Contractual, not just technical, protection Security research touching violence, weapons, exploits Hosted is fine — but supply context in-band Reviewers read text, and context is what distinguishes research from intent Journalling, crisis, intrusive thoughts, ideation Local model, or a human The one class where the pipeline is genuinely adverse to the user's interest That last row is the Florida case in one line. A chat assistant has the affordance of a diary — private-feeling, always available, never bored — and none of its properties. If you want the affordance, run the model on your own machine, where the pipeline does not exist because there is no server. A journal that no classifier ever sees CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ # one-time: install Ollama, then pull a small local model ollama pull llama3.2 # a private journalling session — no network, no review queue, no retention ollama run llama3.2 Everything in that session stays on your disk. See Run Models Locally with Ollama for the full setup and The Private Local AI Stack for the architecture that removes the hosted surface entirely. The other practical move: when your legitimate work genuinely does involve violence, weapons, self-harm or exploitation as subject matter, say so in the conversation. A classifier scores text; a human reviewer reads it. Stated context is the only thing in your control that changes what the reviewer concludes. Give the reviewer the context a classifier cannot infer CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ Context for this conversation, stated up front: I am a [threat analyst / security researcher / novelist / clinician / trust-and-safety engineer] working on [specific artefact: a tabletop exercise, a published paper, chapter 14 of a manuscript, an abuse-detection ruleset]. I need to discuss [violent / self-harm / weapons / exploitation] subject matter as material to be analysed, depicted or detected — not planned. My output is [a report / fiction / a detection rule], not an operational plan. Please keep that frame for the whole thread, and tell me if a request of mine crosses from analysis into operational detail so I can rephrase it. That last line is the useful half. It asks the model to act as a cooperative boundary-keeper rather than leaving you to guess, and a thread containing an explicit refusal-and-rephrase exchange reads very differently to a reviewer than one that does not.

Three over-corrections to avoid, because the discourse around these cases produced all three: It is not continuous surveillance by humans. The human step is reached by a small fraction of conversations routed by classifier, in specific categories. The default experience of every one of these pipelines is that nobody ever reads your chat. It is not new. Content classification plus a human abuse queue plus a narrow legal-referral clause is the standard architecture of every large communications platform, and has been for two decades. What is new is the intimacy of the input — people tell an assistant things they would never post — and the fact that the retention exceptions are now long and written down. It is not unique to one provider. Every table in this page has entries for Anthropic, OpenAI and Google because all three publish the same basic design. Choosing a provider on this axis means comparing specific documented numbers, not vibes. The one real axis of choice is hosted versus local, and Choosing a Model Provider is the page for the rest of that decision. Check yourself 0/6

Anthropic Privacy Policy — section 3, "Recipients and Third-Party Data Sources", is the clause permitting disclosure to government authorities and law enforcement on a good-faith belief it is reasonably necessary to, among other grounds, prevent serious harm to any person or property. Anthropic Usage Policy — the Safeguards Team detection-and-monitoring commitment, the throttle/suspend/terminate enforcement language, the mandatory CSAM reporting obligation, and the scope statement covering anyone who can submit inputs including via resellers and passthrough access. How long do you store my data? — Anthropic privacy centre — the source for immediate removal from history, the 30-day back-end purge, the 5-year de-identified training-pipeline retention, and the critical pair: up to 2 years for flagged inputs and outputs, up to 7 years for trust-and-safety classification scores. Is my data used for model training? — Anthropic privacy centre — the opt-in framing for model improvement, the incognito-chat exclusion, and the statement that conversations flagged for safety review may be used to improve detection and enforcement including training models for the Safeguards team. I have a zero data retention agreement with Anthropic. What products does it apply to? — which products ZDR covers, and the explicit statement that Anthropic still retains User Safety classifier results in order to enforce the Usage Policy. Zero data retention — Claude Code docs — the primary source for the "except where needed to comply with law or combat misuse" carve-out, the 2-year flagged-session retention under ZDR, the table of what ZDR does not cover (claude.ai chat, Cowork, third-party integrations), the per-organisation and forceLoginOrgUUID routing caveats, the features disabled under ZDR, and Covered Model availability. Covered Models — Anthropic support — the model list (Mythos 5.1, Fable 5.1, Mythos 5, Fable 5), the at-least-30-days mandatory retention assessed by automated safety systems, the cross-request-detection rationale, and the Enterprise Frontier Safeguards path for ZDR-eligible customers. Gemini Apps Privacy Hub — Google — human reviewers including trained service providers, the up-to-three-years retention for reviewed chats that survives deleting your activity, the 18-month default auto-delete, the 72-hour window when activity is off, and the explicit instruction not to enter confidential information. Helping people when they need it most — OpenAI — the post containing the specialised-pipeline and law-enforcement-referral language, and the sentence excluding self-harm cases from referral. (The passages are widely quoted; the page blocks automated fetching.) Temporary Chat FAQ — OpenAI help centre — what Temporary Chat removes (history, memory, training) and the safety-retention window of up to 30 days. Also blocks automated fetching; figures here are as reported from that article. Anthropic called SFPD over threat against CEO — The San Francisco Standard, 4 September 2026 — the Friday-to-Tuesday timeline, Anthropic's "safeguards process working as intended" statement, and the user's own account. A Florida Woman Used Claude as a Diary — Decrypt, 5 October 2026 — the Florida case: dates, the automated flag, the human review team, the arrest and the charge. Anthropic reports Florida woman's Claude 'diary' threat — Tom's Hardware — the count of at least three such conversations reaching police since August 2026. Fla. Stat. 836.10, "Written threats to kill, do bodily injury, or conduct a mass shooting or an act of terrorism" — The Florida Senate — the statutory text, including the "in any manner in which it may be viewed by another person" element and the second-degree-felony classification. Related on AILmanac: What AI Chats Leak to Trackers, What Your Agent Uploads, Privacy & Data Handling, Responsible Use, Ethics & Verification.

Privacy & Data Handling — the beginner-level version of the same decision: what is safe to paste, which tier to use, and when the answer is "run it locally." The Private Local AI Stack — the architecture that removes the classifier, the review queue and the retention clock at once, and an honest accounting of the capability you give up. Responsible Use, Ethics & Verification — the other side of the same policy surface: what you are accountable for when the model produces the output. 分享此页面 X LinkedIn Reddit Hacker News 复制链接

用你自己的示例进一步训练模型，使其专门化。通常是最后的手段——先尝试提示词和 RAG。
指示模型 只根据你提供的上下文 来作答——当答案不在其中时就说"我不知道"。它是提示词层面对抗幻觉的主要防线。参见 模式库。
让 AI 行为保持安全且不偏离任务的规则与限制——例如权限规则、"完成前先运行测试"，或对高风险操作要求人工批准。参见 为智能体加固安全。
当模型陈述某件 错误却很自信 的事情。核心技能是核验。参见 幻觉。
在 Claude Code 中，一条在生命周期事件（例如每次文件编辑之后）自动 运行的命令，用于强制执行格式化、关卡校验或安全检查。
运行模型以获得输出的动作（与训练它相对）。
你等待一个回复要花多久。更大的模型通常更慢；流式输出 通过边生成边显示来改善 感知上的 延迟。
Claude 背后的那类 AI：被训练用来 预测下一段文本，而这恰好足以用来写作、编码、总结和推理。参见 什么是 LLM？。
一个用于把 AI 连接到外部工具和数据（数据库、GitHub、浏览器）的 开放标准。一个"MCP 服务器"对外暴露一个工具；Claude 可以调用它。参见 MCP。
一个能处理 不止文本 的模型——例如把图像和 PDF 作为输入。
在 Claude Code 中，一个改变 Claude 沟通方式 的预设（例如简洁、讲解式、学习式），但不改变它能做什么。参见 输出风格。
在 Claude Code 中，它在 不询问 的情况下能做多少——从每次操作都提示，到自动接受编辑。这是速度与安全之间的主要旋钮。参见 权限。
一种只读的 Claude Code 模式，它在 动任何文件之前 先做调研并提出一个计划——你批准之后它才行动。参见 计划模式。
你发给模型的内容：你的指令、问题，以及任何上下文。
在多次调用之间复用提示词中保持不变的前部，以削减成本和延迟。参见 提示词缓存。
一种攻击：隐藏在 AI 所读内容中的恶意指令（一个网页、一份文档）试图劫持它。参见 提示词注入。
从 你的 数据中取出相关片段并加进提示词，让模型基于它们来作答。参见 RAG。
一种模式，模型在回答之前花费额外算力来"思考"，用于更难的任务。在新一代模型上，你可以用 effort 来调节它。
documents.s: 推理 / 扩展思考（Reasoning / extended thinking）

documents.t: 一个打包好的能力（指令 + 可选脚本），Claude 会在相关时 按需 加载它。参见 技能。
Claude Code 中以 / 开头的快捷方式——既有内置的（如 /clear），也有你自己可复用的提示词——它会触发一个已定义的动作。参见 斜杠命令。
让结果以严格、机器可读的形式呈现（例如符合某个 schema 的 JSON），而不是自由文本——这样其他软件就能依赖它们。参见 结构化输出。
一个拥有自身上下文和工具的独立 Claude 实例，用于 委派 一部分任务（例如调研），让主会话保持专注。
为整段对话设定模型角色与规则的高层指令——你最强的引导杠杆。
一个（在某些模型上的）控制随机性的设置：低 = 聚焦且可复现，高 = 多样且有创意。
模型读取并计数的单位——在英语里大约相当于 ¾ 个单词。定价和上下文限额都以 token 计量。参见 Token 与上下文。
让模型调用你定义的函数（搜索、计算器、你的 API）并使用其结果。参见 工具使用。 缺了某个术语？把它加上——术语表条目是绝佳的第一次贡献。 分享此页面 X LinkedIn Reddit Hacker News 复制链接

documents.t: 复制为 Markdown 所有级别 AILmanac 并非孤立存在，我们也不打算取代生态中的一切。这一课是一份坦诚的资源地图，涵盖生态中最好的资源——同样重要的是，告诉你什么时候应该用它们而不是我们。 What you'll learn 明确唯一的事实来源，以及为什么文档与我们不一致时总是以文档为准 认识 Anthropic 的官方资源，以及每一种的用途 了解最好的社区与厂商中立的提示词资源 用一张简单的决策表把任何需求匹配到合适的去处 把 AILmanac 定位为有主见的实战指南
从这里开始，因为其他一切都围绕这条规则运转。 Watch out 当 AILmanac 与官方文档不一致时，以文档为准。需要精确、最新的细节时用文档；需要有主见、分层、边做边学的指导时用我们。 Anthropic 文档 ——关于 Claude、API、模型和功能的权威参考。

这些都是官方一手资源。当你想要权威示例、可运行的代码，或直接来自源头的引导式学习时，就用它们。 提示词最佳实践 ——Anthropic 的提示词参考，按模型给出指导。（它取代了旧的 Prompt Library——一个现成示例提示词的集合，其网址现在会重定向到这里。） Anthropic Cookbook ——可运行的 API 范例（工具调用、RAG、视觉）。 Claude Code 文档 ——CLI/IDE 参考。 Anthropic Academy / Learn ——免费的引导式课程。 Model Context Protocol ——开放的 MCP 标准 + 服务器目录。
当你需要厂商中立的深度内容，或经社区检验的精选工作流时，这些是其中的佼佼者。 awesome-claude-code ——精选的命令、hooks 和工作流。 Prompt Engineering Guide ——深入的、厂商中立的提示词参考。 Learn Prompting ——结构化、对初学者友好的提示词课程。

使用这张地图最快的方法：先从你的需求出发，再跳到对应的去处。 Guided walkthrough1 of 3 1说清你的需求⌄ 确定你此刻真正想要的是什么——精确的规格、可复制粘贴的提示词、可运行的代码、学习路径、理论，还是课程。 ←PreviousNext→ 2在表格里找到匹配项⌄ 在下表左列找到你的需求，再读右列推荐的去处。 ←PreviousNext→ 3在那里深入，然后回来⌄ 用那个资源做深度学习，再回到 AILmanac，沿着有主见、带难度标签的路径把它们串联起来。 ←PreviousNext→ 你想要… 去哪里 精确、最新的 API/功能细节 官方文档 可复制粘贴的示例提示词 Prompt Library / 我们的模板 可运行的 API 代码 Cookbook 有主见、带难度标签的路径 AILmanac 关于提示词的深度理论参考 promptingguide.ai 引导式课程 Anthropic Academy

我们是有主见的实战指南：先给出一种推荐做法，按难度分级，模板丰富，对内容时效坦诚相告，并同时涵盖 Claude 和通用 AI 概念。可以把我们看作一张地图：在合适的时候指向合适的深度资源，并教你基础知识，让这一切都说得通。 自测一下 0/3 Key takeaways Anthropic 官方文档是事实来源——有疑问时，以它为准。 权威示例、代码和课程用官方资源（Prompt Library、Cookbook、Claude Code 文档、Academy、MCP）。 精选工作流和提示词深度用社区与厂商中立资源（awesome-claude-code、promptingguide.ai、Learn Prompting）。 把你的需求匹配到一个去处，然后回到 AILmanac，走有主见、带难度标签的路径。

documents.s: 难度等级与时效性的运作方式

documents.t: 每一页开头都有一个徽章，告诉你它适合谁。下面是全部四种，与它们实际显示的样子完全一致： 入门 不假定任何先备知识。如果你是新手，从这里开始。 进阶 你已经用过一些 AI，想要更深入。 高级 在动手做东西——智能体、API、自定义配置。 所有级别 任何水平都用得上。 徽章依靠的是 文字，而不仅仅是颜色，所以它对每个人都适用（包括屏幕阅读器用户和色盲读者）。跳过高于你水平的内容——或者在你准备好时去挑战它。 Pro tip 想按适合你这类读者的合理顺序，把各个页面串起来阅读？请跟随一条学习路径。 学习路径 会按读者类型，把各个页面以合理的顺序串联起来。

AI 发展很快。任何会变化的内容——模型名称、价格、限额、界面文案、测试版功能——都是 易变事实，在 AILmanac 上它们都带有这样一个标记： 最后验证时间：2026-08-10。 这就是一个时效性标记的样子。日期是某位真人最后一次核查它的时间；链接则是始终具有最终权威的官方来源。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 如何看懂你所见到的内容： 常青页面（像「什么是 LLM」这类概念）不会 带日期——它们不会过时，加日期反而是噪声。 易变页面 会显示日期，让你知道其中的具体内容有多新。 日期偏旧并不是 bug，而是一种诚实。 它在提醒你去复核那一条具体事实，而不是想当然。 Watch out 当日期看起来偏旧时，不要把那个具体数字或文案当成定论——打开链接中的官方来源去确认。来源始终高于页面。

Guided walkthrough1 of 4 1先看徽章⌄ 扫一眼标题下方的徽章。如果它高于你的水平，暂时跳过，或在准备好时去挑战；如果与你匹配，就深入阅读。 ←PreviousNext→ 2查看是否有日期标记⌄ 没有标记意味着该页面是常青的、不会过时。有标记则意味着该页面包含易变事实。 ←PreviousNext→ 3判断日期⌄ 较新的日期意味着其中的具体内容是最新的。偏旧的日期是一个去核验的信号，而不是页面坏掉的标志。 ←PreviousNext→ 4在重要时跟随来源链接⌄ 对任何你将据此行动的内容——价格、限额、模型名称——打开标记中链接的官方来源。它始终为准。 ←PreviousNext→

documents.t: 模型的身份信息只存在于 一个地方——当前模型与价格 表格——并保持核验与标注日期。任何模型事实都不会硬编码在别处；一切都链接到那里。因此，有一个可信赖的单一权威来源。

一份自信满满却内容过时的指南，比没有指南更糟。这些约定让我们既能做到 完整，又不必假装一切都一成不变——也让 你 能够拿捏对任意一行内容该信任多少。 自我检测 0/3 Key takeaways 四种徽章（beginner、intermediate、advanced、all）告诉你一个页面适合谁——而且它们用的是文字，不仅仅是颜色。 易变事实带有「上次核验」日期，外加始终为准的官方来源链接；常青页面不带日期。 偏旧的日期是诚实，不是 bug——去核验，别想当然。 所有模型的身份信息都存放在一个经过核验、标注日期的单一可信来源里：当前模型与价格表格。

documents.s: 欢迎 & 为什么有这个项目

documents.t: 刻意面向所有人——而且我们会标明每一页的难度等级，让你既不会迷失方向，也不会被居高临下地对待： 等级 如果符合以下情况，那就是你…… 入门 你几乎没用过 AI，想要一次稳稳的开门红。 进阶 你已经在用 Claude，希望结果明显更好。 高级 你用 Claude Code、API、智能体和 MCP 进行开发。
已经有很多优秀的资源（参见 全景地图）。AILmanac 不是 一堆链接的堆砌，也不是 对官方文档的照搬。它是： 有主张的——我们先告诉你 唯一推荐的做法，再给出其他备选方案。 标注难度的——每一页都打了标签，让你只读适合自己的内容。 模板丰富的——即拷即用的起步模板，30 秒就能用上。 对时效性诚实的——会变化的事实（模型名称、价格、功能）都附有"上次核验"日期和指向来源的链接。
官方文档才是权威依据 当 AILmanac 与 Anthropic 官方文档 发生冲突时，以官方文档为准。AI 工具变化很快；我们尽力保持最新，但对任何关键内容，请务必对照我们提供的来源链接进行确认。 我们也不会存储你的数据、看不到你的账户，也不会在高风险工作上替你做决定——参见 负责任地使用。

Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1第 1 分钟 —— 打开 Claude⌄ 前往 claude.ai 并登录（免费套餐足以起步）。你也可以在移动 App 上或通过语音使用 Claude——完整对照请看《我该用哪个 Claude？》。 ←PreviousNext→ 2第 2 分钟 —— 像问一位精明的同事那样发问⌄ 不要把它当成“搜索”。给出上下文并说清你想要什么：点明目标、长度、受众、语气，以及“完成”是什么样子。这就占了提示词技巧的 80%，而且它对每一种 AI 都管用。 ←PreviousNext→ 3第 3 分钟 —— 先读，再打磨⌄ 你不必一次就做到完美。用大白话回复即可——“再短一点、更随意些”“在结尾加一句关于免费问答环节的话”。这种一来一回就是迭代式优化。 ←PreviousNext→ 4第 4 分钟 —— 试试第二个、完全不同的任务⌄ 向自己证明它是通用的：总结一篇文章、用浅显的方式解释一个概念，或者用你现有的食材规划一顿快手晚餐。 ←PreviousNext→ 5第 5 分钟 —— 学会那一个安全习惯⌄ AI 可能听起来很自信却依然是错的。对任何重要的内容，都要核查它。核实事实、数字、日期、引语和引用出处。 ←PreviousNext→

第一天最大的胜利：给出上下文，并说清你想要什么。对比一下： ❌ “营销邮件” ✅ “写一封友好的、120 字的邮件，邀请现有客户参加 6 月 30 日关于我们新数据分析仪表盘的网络研讨会。语气温暖但不要推销味。结尾给出一个清晰的报名行动号召。” 第二个提示词点明了目标、字数、受众、语气，以及“完成”是什么样子。这就占了提示词技巧的 80%，而且它在每一种 AI 上都管用。（更多内容见提示词基础。） 可以试试的第一个提示词 CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ Write a friendly 120-word email inviting existing customers to a webinar on June 30 about our new analytics dashboard. Warm but not salesy. End with a clear RSVP call to action.

documents.t: Python TypeScript import time, random, anthropic client = anthropic.Anthropic() def ask(messages, model="claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens=1024, system=None): for attempt in range(5): try: return client.messages.create( model=model, max_tokens=max_tokens, system=system or anthropic.NOT_GIVEN, messages=messages, ) except (anthropic.RateLimitError, anthropic.APIStatusError) as e: if attempt == 4: raise time.sleep(min(2 ** attempt + random.random(), 30)) import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk"; const client = new Anthropic(); export async function ask(messages, { model = "claude-sonnet-5", maxTokens = 1024, system } = {}) { for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 5; attempt++) { try { return await client.messages.create({ model, max_tokens: maxTokens, system, messages }); } catch (e: any) { if (attempt === 4 || ![429, 500, 529].includes(e?.status)) throw e; await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, Math.min(2 ** attempt * 1000 + Math.random() * 1000, 30000))); } } } （SDK 默认也会对瞬时错误进行重试 —— 在叠加自己的重试逻辑之前，先了解你所用客户端的行为。参见错误与速率限制。）

# Project: <name> (Next.js + TypeScript) ## How to run - Dev: `npm run dev` - Build: `npm run build` - Test: `npm test` - Lint: `npm run lint` (must pass before commit) ## Conventions - TypeScript strict; no `any` without a comment justifying it. - Components in `src/components`, one folder per component. - Data fetching via tRPC; never call the DB from a client component. - Styling: Tailwind utility classes; no inline styles. ## Guardrails - After any change, run `npm run lint && npm test`. - Keep files under ~300 lines; split when larger. - Do not modify `prisma/migrations` by hand.

# Project: <name> (FastAPI) ## How to run - Install: `uv sync` (or `pip install -e .`) - Dev: `uvicorn app.main:app --reload` - Test: `pytest` - Lint/format: `ruff check . && ruff format .` ## Conventions - Type hints everywhere; prefer `pathlib` over `os.path`. - Pydantic models for all request/response bodies. - f-strings, not %-formatting. ## Guardrails - Run `pytest` and `ruff check` before completing a task. - Fail fast with descriptive errors; no silent excepts.

note if it's pure server-side templates instead - Frontend: HTMX + Alpine.js / React SPA # pick one; state the truth - Key packages: django-environ, Pillow, whitenoise ## Settings layout # config/ # settings/ # base.py ← shared # local.py ← DEBUG=True, console email backend # production.py← env-driven secrets, ALLOWED_HOSTS, SECURE_* flags # Load via DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE env var. ## How to run - Install: `pip install -e ".[dev]"` or `uv sync` - Env file: copy `.env.example` → `.env` and fill secrets - Migrate: `python manage.py migrate` - Dev server: `python manage.py runserver` - Shell: `python manage.py shell_plus` # django-extensions - Test: `pytest` (pytest-django; see pytest.ini) - Lint/format: `ruff check . && ruff format .` - Type check: `mypy .` # if mypy is configured ## Project layout <project_slug>/ <app_name>/ models.py # one model family per app; no god-models views.py # CBVs preferred; FBVs for simple one-offs serializers.py # DRF only urls.py # app-level URL conf; included from config/urls.py services.py # business logic lives here, NOT in views or models tasks.py # Celery tasks tests/ test_models.py test_views.py config/ settings/ urls.py wsgi.py / asgi.py manage.py ## Conventions ### Models - Fat service layer, thin models: domain logic goes in `services.py`, not model methods. - Always set `verbose_name` and `verbose_name_plural` on Meta. - Use `get_object_or_404` or `select_related`/`prefetch_related` — never N+1 queries. - UUID primary keys for all user-facing models: `id = models.UUIDField(primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4, editable=False)`. ### Migrations - One migration per logical change; never squash without team sign-off. - Never edit a migration that has been applied to staging or production. - Name meaningful ones: `python manage.py makemigrations --name add_published_at_to_post`. ### Views & URLs - Class-Based Views for CRUD and list/detail; Function-Based Views for anything with unusual branching. - DRF ViewSets for API endpoints; routers in `<app>/urls.py`. - All URLs namespaced: `app_name = "blog"` in each app's `urls.py`. ### Templates (if server-side rendered) - Extend `base.html`; block names: `title`, `content`, `extra_css`, `extra_js`. - No business logic in templates; use template tags or pass computed context from the view. ### Security - `SECRET_KEY` and all credentials via environment variables (django-environ); never hardcoded. - CSRF on all mutating endpoints; DRF uses `SessionAuthentication` + CSRF by default. - `SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT`, `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`, `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE` = True in production. ## Guardrails - Run `pytest && ruff check .` before marking any task done. - Never edit applied migrations; create a new one instead. - Do not add raw SQL unless there is no ORM equivalent — document why if you do. - Do not import from `django.conf.settings` inside model files; pass values explicitly. - After adding a new dependency, update `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements/*.txt`) and note it here. ## Good to know - `DEBUG=True` in local; `DEBUG=False` in all server environments — never skip this. - Static files are served by WhiteNoise in production; run `collectstatic` before deploy. - Celery worker: `celery -A config worker -l info`; beat: `celery -A config beat -l info`. - <Add any project-specific gotchas: custom user model, multi-tenancy, third-party integrations.>

pick one - HTTP: Axum / Actix-web # remove unused - Serialisation: serde + serde_json - Database: sqlx (async, compile-time checked queries) # remove if unused - Error handling: thiserror (library) / anyhow (binary) # pick per crate type - Key crates: tracing, tracing-subscriber, dotenvy ## How to run - Build (dev): `cargo build` - Build (rel): `cargo build --release` - Test: `cargo test` - Lint: `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` - Format: `cargo fmt --check` - Docs: `cargo doc --open` - Watch: `cargo watch -x test` # remove if unused ## Workspace layout (if multi-crate) Cargo.toml # [workspace] root crates/ core/ # domain logic, no I/O, no async api/ # Axum HTTP layer db/ # sqlx repository layer cli/ # binary entry-point ## Conventions - No `unwrap()` or `expect()` in library crates; propagate with `?`. - `expect()` in binaries only where a panic is truly unrecoverable — with a message explaining why. - Prefer `thiserror` for library error enums; `anyhow` for binary/main error chains. - Async only at the edges (HTTP handlers, DB calls); keep domain logic sync. - Derive `Debug`, `Clone`, `serde::Serialize/Deserialize` where it makes sense. - Feature flags in `Cargo.toml` for optional integrations; document each one. ## Guardrails - Run `cargo test && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check` before done. - Never silence a Clippy lint without a `#[allow(...)]` comment explaining why. - Do not use `unsafe` without a `// SAFETY:` comment justifying it. - Do not add a crate that duplicates one already in the dependency tree without discussion. - Keep compile times in mind: prefer concrete types over heavy generics in hot paths. ## Good to know - `sqlx` queries are checked at compile time — run `cargo sqlx prepare` to update the offline cache after changing queries. - MSRV is enforced in CI; do not use features newer than the stated MSRV. - <Add project-specific gotchas: WASM target, FFI boundaries, no_std constraints.>

每条规则都对应本站上一个更深入的页面： 检查项 为什么重要 足以让其行动 一行的提示词会迫使 Claude 去猜测你的意图。 设定角色 “你是一位资深的 X”能够清晰地聚焦语气和判断力——参见 角色。 陈述一个明确的任务 一个开头的祈使动词（“总结……”、“提取……”）能消除歧义。 指定输出形态 没有格式，你得到的长度和结构就由 Claude 自行决定——参见 结构化输出。 给出示例 对于模式类任务，一对输入→输出胜过大段的描述——参见 少样本。 较长时进行结构化 长提示词需要 XML 标签，这样 Claude 才能区分指令与内容。 防范编造的答案 当你提供源文本时，告诉 Claude 只使用它——这是对抗 幻觉 的核心防线。 避免含糊的修饰词 “好”、“吸引人”、“专业”都无法衡量。请用可检验的标准替换它们。 从评分到交付 高分并不是目标——可靠的结果才是。把脚手架当作一个起点，然后在依赖输出之前用一次真实的 评估 来证明它。

documents.t: 运行 /init 来起草一份 CLAUDE.md，然后精简它，只保留真正成立的内容：技术栈、如何运行/测试/检查代码、真实的约定，以及护栏规则（"完成前先跑测试"、"不要碰 /generated"）。*原因：*它是杠杆率最高的定制项 —— Claude 每个会话都会读取它。 可以从 CLAUDE.md 模板 拿一份起步模板。

documents.t: 添加一个 .claude/settings.json（参考），预先放行安全、重复的命令，并拒绝危险的命令： { "permissions": { "allow": ["Read", "Bash(npm run test:*)", "Bash(npm run lint)", "Bash(git diff:*)"], "ask": ["Write", "Bash(npm install:*)"], "deny": ["Read(./.env)", "Bash(git push --force:*)"] } } *原因：*在安全操作上减少打断，在有风险的操作上硬性叫停。参见 权限。
documents.s: 第 2 步 — 设置权限

documents.t: 在每次编辑后自动格式化（钩子）： { "hooks": { "PostToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Edit|Write", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "f=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path'); npx prettier --write \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || true" } ] } ] } } *原因：*确保格式一致 —— 而不是"麻烦记得格式化一下"。
documents.s: 第 3 步 — 添加一个格式化钩子

documents.t: 把 斜杠命令库 里的 /commit 配方放进 .claude/commands/。*原因：*用一个词触发一套可复用的工作流。
documents.s: 第 4 步 — 添加一个 /commit 命令

documents.t: 在 计划模式 中给出一个真实目标，审阅计划，然后让它执行。*原因：*通过把思考和执行分开来建立信任。
documents.s: 第 5 步 — 用计划模式来完成第一个真实任务
documents.h: #第-5-步--用计划模式来完成第一个真实任务

documents.t: 新会话 → Claude 无需提示就引用了你的约定（CLAUDE.md 生效）。 编辑一个文件 → 它被自动格式化（钩子生效）。 一个有风险的命令 → 它会询问或拒绝（权限生效）。 /commit → 一条干净的约定式提交（Conventional Commit）信息（命令生效）。

documents.s: 构建并接入你的第一个 MCP 服务器

documents.t: 一个带有单个工具 word_count 的 stdio 服务器，Claude 可以调用它。同样的模式可以扩展到"查询我的数据库"、"开一个工单"等等。

server.py（Python；TypeScript 版本见 MCP 脚手架）： from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP mcp = FastMCP("text-tools") @mcp.tool() def word_count(text: str) -> int: """Count the words in a piece of text.""" return len(text.split()) if __name__ == "__main__": mcp.run() # stdio transport
把它添加到仓库根目录的 .mcp.json 中： { "mcpServers": { "text-tools": { "command": "python", "args": ["server.py"] } } }
在仓库中启动 Claude Code。问它："用 text-tools 服务器统计这段文字的词数：'the quick brown fox'。" Claude 应该会调用 word_count 并报告 4。如果它看不到这个工具，请检查服务器能否独立干净地启动，以及 .mcp.json 的路径是否正确。
documents.s: 第 3 步 — 连接并测试

documents.t: 把 word_count 替换成你实际的能力 —— 一次数据库查询、一次内部 API 调用、一次文件操作。加入输入校验，并把错误作为结果返回。
documents.s: 第 4 步 — 让它真正可用

documents.t: 服务器 = 代码 + 访问权限 最小权限 —— 只给它所需的数据/操作（保护 Agent）。 校验模型发来的输入。 它返回的不可信数据可能携带 提示词注入。 在连接任何第三方服务器之前，先审查它。

documents.t: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..." # never in source control 把模型 ID 放在配置里，而不是散落在各处的字面量中，这样迁移就变得轻而易举（原因）。要慎重选择 —— 选择模型。

documents.h: #第-1-步--从配置中读取密钥与模型

documents.t: Python TypeScript import os, time, random, anthropic client = anthropic.Anthropic() MODEL = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_MODEL", "claude-sonnet-5") def ask_stream(prompt, system=None, max_tokens=1024): for attempt in range(5): try: with client.messages.stream( model=MODEL, max_tokens=max_tokens, system=system or anthropic.NOT_GIVEN, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], ) as stream: for text in stream.text_stream: print(text, end="", flush=True) final = stream.get_final_message() print() usage = final.usage print(f"\n[tokens in/out: {usage.input_tokens}/{usage.output_tokens}]") return final except (anthropic.RateLimitError, anthropic.APIStatusError): if attempt == 4: raise time.sleep(min(2 ** attempt + random.random(), 30)) import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk"; const client = new Anthropic(); const MODEL = process.env.CLAUDE_MODEL ?? "claude-sonnet-5"; export async function askStream(prompt: string, system?: string, maxTokens = 1024) { for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 5; attempt++) { try { const stream = client.messages.stream({ model: MODEL, max_tokens: maxTokens, system, messages: [{ role: "user", content: prompt }] }); for await (const e of stream) if (e.type === "content_block_delta") process.stdout.write(e.delta.text ?? ""); const final = await stream.finalMessage(); console.error(`\n[tokens in/out: ${final.usage.input_tokens}/${final.usage.output_tokens}]`); return final; } catch (e: any) { if (attempt === 4 || ![429, 500, 529].includes(e?.status)) throw e; await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, Math.min(2 ** attempt * 1000, 30000))); } } }

documents.t: 记录 token 用量（如上），这样你就能看清每次调用的开销。 合理设置 max_tokens 和模型；用精炼的提示词控制输入。 对于反复出现的稳定前缀，启用 提示词缓存。 参见 Token 与定价 和 成本与延迟。

documents.s: 端到端编写你的第一个技能

documents.t: mkdir -p .claude/skills/changelog-entry （如果想要一个跨所有项目的个人技能，请使用 ~/.claude/skills/…。）
documents.s: 第 1 步 — 创建文件夹

documents.t: .claude/skills/changelog-entry/SKILL.md： --- name: changelog-entry description: Use when the user wants to turn recent git commits into a Keep a Changelog entry. --- # Changelog Entry When asked for a changelog entry: 1. Run `git log --oneline -20` to see recent commits. 2. Group them into Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed (Keep a Changelog style). 3. Write concise, user-facing bullets (not raw commit messages). 4. Output only the formatted entry. description 就是触发器 —— 把它写成"Use when…（当……时使用）"的形式，这样 Claude 才会在合适的时机加载它。
documents.s: 第 2 步 — 编写 SKILL.md

documents.t: 技能可以附带脚本。如果你想要确定性的数据收集，可以添加 scripts/recent.sh 并在 SKILL.md 中引用它： #!/usr/bin/env bash git log --oneline -20
documents.s: 第 3 步 —（可选）添加一个辅助脚本
documents.h: #第-3-步-可选添加一个辅助脚本

documents.t: 启动一个会话并说："为最近的工作起草一条 changelog 条目。" Claude 应该识别出意图，加载该技能，并按照它的步骤执行。如果它没有被激活，多半是你的 description 对何时使用它描述得不够具体 —— 把它写得更精准些。
documents.s: 第 4 步 — 验证它能被触发

documents.t: 把它（连同其他技能）打包成一个 插件，让你的团队一步就能安装 —— 或者把它贡献给 AILmanac 的 技能包。
描述含糊 → 永远不触发（或者总是触发）。要具体。 一个技能里塞太多东西 → 让它专注于一件清晰的工作。 共享技能中含有密钥 → 绝不可以；参见 审查第三方代码。

复制为 Markdown 高级 把大型任务拆分给多个聚焦的 子智能体，比把所有内容塞进一个上下文要好得多。让我们设计一条 研究 → 实现 → 审查 的流水线。
documents.s: 设计一个多子智能体工作流

documents.t: 每个子智能体都有自己的上下文和量身定制的工具集 —— 而且只有结果会流回主会话，从而让主会话保持干净。
通过 /agents 界面定义三个智能体，每个都配以紧凑的 description（以便主智能体能正确委派任务）和受限的工具集： researcher（研究者） —— 仅可读取/搜索。梳理相关代码并返回发现。 implementer（实现者） —— 可以编辑文件并运行测试；将研究者的发现作为输入。 reviewer（审查者） —— 只读、对抗性：查找 bug、遗漏的情况以及违反约定之处。
documents.s: 第 1 步 — 定义这些智能体

documents.t: 主会话将每个阶段的输出传递给下一个阶段：研究 → 实现（利用研究成果）→ 审查（针对实现）。加入一道审查关卡：如果审查者发现了问题，就在收尾之前回到实现者那里重新循环。
documents.s: 第 2 步 — 通过交接进行编排

documents.t: 并行/多智能体并非没有代价 顺序依赖（实现需要研究）必须保持顺序执行 —— 不要在顺序至关重要的地方做并行扇出。 共享文件写入可能会发生冲突 —— 用 git worktree 隔离，或者串行执行。 对于小任务，协调开销会超过收益。请将此用于规模较大、可拆解的工作。
documents.s: 第 3 步 — 知道什么时候不该这样做
documents.h: #第-3-步--知道什么时候不该这样做

documents.t: 一次好的多智能体运行应当呈现：一个聚焦的主上下文（繁重的阅读发生在研究者那里）、一份反映了研究成果的实现，以及一次确实发现了问题（或者可信地给出了通过结论）的审查。如果审查者只是橡皮图章，就把它的提示词改得更对抗性一些（"努力找出哪里有问题"）。
把同样的模式以编程方式实现，就是 在 API 上构建 Agent，以及诸如 Cowork 与 Agent 团队 这样的产品形态。

复制为 Markdown 高级 最后验证时间：2026-06-20。 无头模式的标志位和 CI 集成细节会不断演进 —— 请对照官方的 Claude Code / Agent SDK 文档进行确认。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 一个经典的高价值自动化：让 Claude 审查每一个拉取请求，并把它的发现作为评论发布出来 —— 在 CI 中以 无头模式 运行。下面是它的整体形态，以及保障其安全的护栏。
documents.s: 审查每一个 PR 的 GitHub Action

documents.t: 在每个 PR 上：检出 diff，让 Claude 审查其中的 bug/边界情况/约定问题，然后发布一条评论。最终仍由人类决定；Claude 只是提供一次快速的初审。

name: Claude PR review on: pull_request permissions: contents: read pull-requests: write # to comment — NOT write to code jobs: review: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: { fetch-depth: 0 } - name: Review the diff env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }} run: | git diff origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD > /tmp/diff.patch claude -p "Review this diff for correctness bugs, missing edge cases, and security issues. Report ONLY high-confidence findings as a Markdown checklist with file:line. Diff:" < /tmp/diff.patch > /tmp/review.md # then post /tmp/review.md as a PR comment (e.g. with the gh CLI or an action) （具体的无头调用方式可能有所不同 —— 请参阅文档。原理是：喂入 diff，捕获 Markdown，然后发布出去。）

CI 中的最小权限原则 只评论。 授予 pull-requests: write，而不是 contents: write —— 这个机器人不应推送代码。 限定 token 的作用范围；绝不要把部署/密钥访问权限暴露给一个读取不可信 PR 内容的任务。 将 PR 内容视为不可信 —— 它可能携带 提示词注入；不要让该任务执行有后果的操作。 控制成本 —— 大型 diff 会消耗 token；可以考虑只审查发生变更的文件。
documents.s: 护栏（请阅读 加固自主运行）

documents.t: 只要求高置信度的发现 —— 一大堆吹毛求疵的意见只会被忽略。 把它定位为一次初审，由人类做出是否合并的决定。
documents.s: 让它有用，而不是制造噪音

复制为 Markdown 进阶 最后验证时间：2026-11-02。 弃用时间表和迁移细节来自 Anthropic 且会发生变化——在迁移之前，请务必在官方文档中确认日期和替代方案。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 模型会被退役，参数会被重命名，行为会发生变化。本页追踪 破坏性变更，让升级不会让你措手不及。如果你基于 API 进行构建，请定期浏览本页。
一个被固定的模型 ID 终将被 弃用，进而被 移除。硬编码该 ID 的代码会出问题。一点点保养就能避免凌晨两点的意外。
从配置中读取模型 ID，绝不要在整个代码库中散布字面量——这样迁移就只是改动一行。 关注公告，留意弃用日期和推荐的替代方案。 切换模型时，重新运行你的 评估——即使是在“更新、更好”的模型上，行为也可能发生变化。 在截止日期之前测试，而不是在移除之后。
变更 示例 应对方式 模型退役 某个较旧的模型 ID 停止工作 迁移到推荐的后继模型；重新评估 参数被取代 某个推理/预算旋钮被 effort 取代 更新调用；参阅 思考与 Effort 默认值变更 新的默认模型/行为 有意识地固定版本；验证你的提示词是否仍然有效 端点/SDK 更新 新的 SDK 主版本 阅读迁移指南；谨慎升级
权威的时间表位于官方模型弃用页面——在迁移之前，请在那里确认日期。Anthropic 会在退役某个公开发布的模型之前提供至少 60 天的提前通知。

目前有一个公开发布的 Claude 模型处于“已弃用但尚未退役”的窗口期（2026年11月2日核对）：claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929（Sonnet 4.5）已于 2026年9月30日弃用，并将于 2026年11月30日退役。 Anthropic 推荐的替代模型是 claude-sonnet-5-5。调用在退役日期之前照常工作，之后就会失败——如果你的代码里还固定着这个 ID，这就是你要做的迁移，现在这个窗口还剩不到四周。 同样已弃用：仅限邀请的 claude-mythos-preview（2026年6月9日弃用，退役日期待公布）——请迁移到当前需要通过验证才能使用的模型 claude-mythos-5-1。（claude-mythos-5 仍为 Active，但它有自己的迁移指南，指向 5.1，所以迁移两次是白费功夫。） claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 是下一个要留意的 ID，它现在是产品线中唯一一个已经越过最早可能退役日期的模型：那个下限是 2026年10月15日，现已过去（下一个是 Opus 4.5 的，在 2026年11月24日）。它还被列在模型概览的旧版（legacy）模型之中，直接后继是 claude-haiku-5-5（2026年10月7日发布）。截至 2026年11月2日，官方状态表仍将其列为 Active，且尚未宣布弃用，所以这两种说法并不矛盾：在 Anthropic 自己的生命周期术语里，“legacy”的意思是不再接收更新，未来可能被弃用，比“已弃用”低一档。“不早于”的日期到达只是提示你该做规划，而不是故障——Anthropic 承诺至少提前 60 天通知，而这 60 天是从通知发出时开始算的，不是从下限日期越过时开始算。Sonnet 4.5 就是现成的例子：它的下限日期是 2026年9月29日，弃用通知在9月30日发出，而真正的退役在那之后两个月。如果你固定使用这个 ID，现在这次迁移值得排进日程，而不只是观望——而且它不只是换个 ID：请参阅 Claude Haiku 5.5：100K 价格悬崖，了解会返回 400 的五项变更和仍返回 200 的六项变更。迁移前请在官方模型状态表中确认。

claude-opus-4-1-20250805（Opus 4.1）已于 2026年8月5日退役——请迁移到 claude-opus-4-8（或直接迁移到 claude-opus-5）。 claude-opus-4-20250514（Opus 4）和 claude-sonnet-4-20250514（Sonnet 4）已于 2026年6月15日退役——Anthropic 列出的替代模型分别是 claude-opus-4-8 和 claude-sonnet-4-6（或直接迁移到 claude-opus-5 / claude-sonnet-5）。 对任何已退役 ID 的调用现在都会返回 API 错误。如果你的代码仍然固定使用其中之一，那就是第一件要修的事。

采样旋钮 temperature、top_p 和 top_k 正在被逐步淘汰，而且现在根据你发送的 API 版本不同，有两套不同的规则。 使用 anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 时（2026年10月21日之前发布的所有 SDK 主版本都发送这个版本）：在 Claude 4.7 代及更高版本的模型（Opus 4.7、Opus 4.8、Opus 5、Opus 5.5、Sonnet 5、Sonnet 5.5、Haiku 5.5、Fable 5、Fable 5.1、Mythos 5、Mythos 5.1）以及 Claude Mythos Preview 上，将其中任何一个设置为非默认值都会返回 400 错误。默认值会被接受，较旧的模型仍然接受非默认值。请看版本号而不是名字：Haiku 5.5 会拒绝非默认的采样值，而较旧的 Haiku 4.5 仍然接受，Opus 4.6 和 Sonnet 4.6 也一样。 使用 anthropic-version: 2026-10-21 时：这三个参数已被移除。发送其中任何一个，在所有模型上都会返回 400，即使取的是该参数的默认值。最新的 SDK 主版本和 ant CLI 已把它们从请求类型和命令行标志中删除。 无论哪种情况，解决办法都一样：三个参数全部省略，改用提示词和思考与 Effort 来引导行为。唯一没有替代方案的情形，是在仍然遵守该参数的较旧模型上有意调低温度——Anthropic 文档给出的选项是停止发送该参数，或让该请求继续使用 2023-06-01。关于你当前使用的是哪个版本、以及随之还有哪些变化的完整说明：API Version 2026-10-21。 请始终对照 当前模型与定价 表格确认你的模型 ID；如果你仍在使用较旧的 ID，请规划一次迁移。

AILmanac's one promise is to be honest about freshness. Most docs sites say they're current; this page proves it. Every page below is scored against its last verification date — computed against your clock, right now, so this dashboard can never quietly go stale itself. This is the easiest way to contribute See a page marked 🔴 Stale or ⚪ Unverified? That's an open invitation. Click Verify, check the page against its official source, and add (or bump) its <VerifyNote lastVerified="YYYY-MM-DD" />. One date is a complete, welcome contribution — see Contribute in 10 Minutes.

🟢 Fresh — verified within the last 90 days. 🟡 Aging — verified 90–180 days ago; worth a glance. 🔴 Stale — verified over 180 days ago; likely drifted from the source. ⚪ Unverified — no <VerifyNote> yet. Volatile pages (model names, prices, limits, UI labels) should always carry one. The data is rebuilt from the docs on every site build by scripts/build-freshness.mjs, which reads each page's most recent <VerifyNote lastVerified="…"> stamp. Nothing to maintain by hand — add a stamp to a page and it shows up here automatically.

Last verified: 2026-11-02 · Official models & pricing Model API model ID Tier Best for Claude Fable 5.1 claude-fable-5-1 Mythos-classflagship (above Opus) Released September 1, 2026. For demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, or when Opus 5.5 at higher effort still falls short on your evals — Anthropic's models overview recommends starting with Opus 5.5 for most workloads and reaching for Fable 5.1 only when it falls short. Same list price as Fable 5 with cache reads at a quarter of the cost. Three breaking changes vs Fable 5: forced tool_choice (any/tool) returns 400, thinking blocks are readable only by Fable 5.1 or newer, and editing earlier turns invalidates thinking blocks. Refuses in-band (HTTP 200, stop_reason: refusal); fallback targets are Opus 5 and Opus 4.8. 30-day retention (not ZDR-eligible unless expressly authorized by Anthropic); not on Priority Tier. (Supersedes Claude Fable 5, now a legacy model.) 展开 Claude Mythos 5.1 claude-mythos-5-1 Mythos-classverification required Same capabilities, specs and pricing as Fable 5.1, available only to organizations verified through Anthropic's verification programs. Since October 6, 2026 that is an application, not an invitation: Project Glasswing was restructured into the Cyber Verification Program's three tiers — Defense Access (organizations, and individuals on paid plans), Red Team Access (organizations only) and Specialized Access (organizations only, reviewed with the US government, where Glasswing members landed) — each granting Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Mythos 5.1. Apply at portal.anthropic.com/programs; decisions typically within seven business days. Does not run the conversation-binding check on thinking blocks. Customers without access should use Fable 5.1. 展开 Claude Opus 5.5 claude-opus-5-5 Opusmost capable Anthropic's recommended starting point for most workloads, released September 22, 2026: long-running agentic coding and knowledge work, 1M context, 128k output, June 2026 reliable knowledge cutoff. Beats the larger Fable 5.1 on every row of Anthropic's launch table at 40% of its list price. Default effort is 'medium' (shared only with Haiku 5.5 — every other model that supports effort defaults to 'high'), and at a given level it thinks more per turn than Opus 5 — re-run your effort sweep instead of carrying settings over. Four breaking changes vs Opus 5: thinking cannot be disabled at any effort level (400), forced tool_choice (any/tool) returns 400 including on token counting, thinking blocks are bound to both the model and the conversation prefix, and computer_20251124 is rejected on the Claude API and Google Cloud (still accepted on Bedrock). A fifth change returns 200: text between tool calls now arrives in progress-update thinking blocks, empty at the default display of 'omitted'. Refuses in-band (HTTP 200, stop_reason: refusal) with new 'bio' and 'reasoning_extraction' categories; server-side fallback does NOT retry 'reasoning_extraction'. Fast mode is Claude API only. Retirement no sooner than September 22, 2027. (Supersedes Claude Opus 5, now a legacy model.) 展开 Claude Opus 5 claude-opus-5 Opusmost capable Legacy since September 22, 2026 (superseded by Opus 5.5) but still available. Complex agentic coding and enterprise work, 1M context, 128k output. Two reasons to stay on it for now: it accepts thinking: {type: 'disabled'} at 'high' effort or below, and its thinking blocks are readable by more models than Opus 5.5's (only Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 read Opus 5.5's). (Supersedes Claude Opus 4.8, now a legacy model.) 展开 Claude Sonnet 5.5 claude-sonnet-5-5 Sonnetbalanced The best combination of speed and intelligence, released September 28, 2026: well-scoped everyday tasks, bug fixes, multistep tool use and polished documents, 1M context, 128k output (300k on Batches with a beta header), June 2026 reliable knowledge cutoff. Exactly Sonnet 5's prices and the same tokenizer, yet Anthropic claims output 30%+ faster and up to 30% less per task — the saving is in the token and turn counts, not the rate card. Beats Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (70.6% vs 66.4%) and ties it on knowledge-work Elo, but trails it by ~8 points on FrontierCode 1.1. Default effort is 'high' and levels are recalibrated — re-run your sweep. Minimum cacheable prompt drops to 512 tokens (1,024 on Sonnet 5). Five breaking changes vs Sonnet 5: thinking: {type: 'disabled'} returns 400 (use 'between_tools', accepted only at 'high' effort or below and with no companion field), forced tool_choice (any/tool) returns 400 including on token counting, thinking blocks are bound to the model, the conversation prefix and the producing account, computer_20251124 is rejected on the Claude API and Google Cloud (still accepted on Bedrock), and Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 / Sonnet 5 are rejected as advisor-tool advisors. A sixth change returns 200: text between tool calls arrives in progress-update thinking blocks, empty at the default display of 'omitted'. Refuses in-band (HTTP 200, stop_reason: refusal) in five categories; server-side fallback retries only 'cyber' and 'frontier_llm', on Sonnet 5. temperature/top_p/top_k at non-default values return 400. Retirement no sooner than September 28, 2027. (Supersedes Claude Sonnet 5, now a legacy model.) 展开 Claude Sonnet 5 claude-sonnet-5 Sonnetbalanced Legacy since September 28, 2026 (superseded by Sonnet 5.5) but still available. The balanced pick when speed and cost matter more than Opus-level depth, 1M context. Two reasons to stay on it for now: it accepts thinking: {type: 'disabled'} at any effort level including 'xhigh' and 'max' (Sonnet 5.5's 'between_tools' tops out at 'high'), and it supports forced tool_choice, which Sonnet 5.5 does not. It is also the server-side fallback target for Sonnet 5.5's 'cyber' and 'frontier_llm' refusals. (Supersedes Claude Sonnet 4.6, now a legacy model.) 展开 Claude Haiku 5.5 claude-haiku-5-5 Haikufastest & cheapest The fastest model, released October 7, 2026: high-volume, latency-sensitive work — classification, extraction, routing, and cheap sub-agents. 1M context (up from Haiku 4.5's 200k), 128k output (up from 64k, 300k on Batches with a beta header), June 2026 reliable knowledge cutoff (up from Feb 2025), and the first Haiku with adaptive thinking and the effort parameter (default 'medium'). THE ONLY CURRENT MODEL PRICED BY PROMPT LENGTH: every other 4.6-and-later model bills the full 1M window at standard rates, but Haiku 5.5 has two rate cards split at 100,000 tokens, and crossing that line reprices the WHOLE request — input, output, cache writes, cache reads and batch — at 5x. It also moves to the newer tokenizer, so the same text counts ~30% more tokens than on Haiku 4.5: the real saving is ~87% below the cliff and ~35% above it, not the 90% on the rate card. Five breaking changes vs Haiku 4.5: budget_tokens thinking returns 400, non-default temperature/top_p/top_k return 400, assistant prefill returns 400 even with thinking off, computer_20250124 is rejected on the Claude API and Google Cloud, and sending thinking blocks back after editing earlier turns returns 400. Unusually permissive where the bigger 5.5 models are not — it accepts both thinking: {type: 'disabled'} (at 'high' effort or below) and forced tool_choice, which Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 both reject. Refuses in-band (HTTP 200, stop_reason: refusal) in four categories with NO server-side fallback. Priority Tier is not supported. Retirement no sooner than October 7, 2027. (Supersedes Claude Haiku 4.5, now a legacy model.) 展开 Claude Haiku 4.5 claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 Haikufastest & cheapest Legacy since October 7, 2026 (superseded by Haiku 5.5) but still available, and still the only model with a 200k context window (not 1M), a 64k output cap, and no support for the effort parameter; its reliable knowledge cutoff is Feb 2025. Three reasons to stay on it for now: it accepts assistant prefill and manual extended thinking (budget_tokens), both of which Haiku 5.5 rejects with a 400, and it supports Priority Tier, which Haiku 5.5 does not. It is also flat-rated — Haiku 5.5's cheaper price applies only to prompts up to 100,000 tokens. Watch its lifecycle closely: its earliest-possible retirement date of October 15, 2026 has now PASSED, so it can be deprecated at any time — yet as of November 2, 2026 the status table still lists it Active with no deprecation announced. It is the only current model past its floor (Opus 4.5 is next, on November 24, 2026) and it now has a direct successor. This is a signal to plan, not an outage: Anthropic commits to at least 60 days' notice once a deprecation is announced, so a migration started now has room. 展开 Claude Fable 5 claude-fable-5 Mythos-classflagship (above Opus) Legacy since September 1, 2026 (superseded by Fable 5.1) but still available. Multiday autonomous runs, first-shot on ambiguous specs, dense vision, sustained delegation to parallel subagents. GA June 9 2026. Refuses in-band (HTTP 200, stop_reason: refusal) — configure server-side or client-side fallback. Adaptive thinking only; raw thinking never returned. 30-day retention (NOT ZDR-eligible). Two reasons to stay on it for now: it supports forced tool_choice and Priority Tier (existing commitments only — new ones are no longer sold), which Fable 5.1 does not. 展开 Claude Mythos 5 claude-mythos-5 Mythos-classverification required, legacy Superseded by Mythos 5.1. Shares Fable 5's specs and pricing, offered separately for defensive cybersecurity workflows to organizations verified through Anthropic's verification programs — originally the invite-only Project Glasswing. Since October 6, 2026 the way in is an application to the Cyber Verification Program, and what its tiers grant is Mythos 5.1, not this model. Customers without access should use Fable 5.1. 展开 Model IDs are exact; tiers and 'best for' are guidance. Pricing, context-window sizes and rate limits change frequently and are intentionally NOT listed here — always read them on the official page above. documents.t: 一条快速的经验法则（完整指导见 选择模型）： 从 Sonnet 开始。 对大多数工作而言，它在质量、速度和成本之间达到了最佳平衡。 当难题上的质量比成本更重要时，选用 Opus。 对于高并发、对延迟敏感或简单的任务，降级到 Haiku。

复制为 Markdown 所有级别 最后验证时间：2026-06-24。 本页是一份持续滚动、由人工策划的摘要。如需权威、完整的变更列表，请始终查阅 Anthropic 官方文档和 Claude Code 更新日志。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 用通俗易懂的语言总结 Claude 近期在各方面的变化——让你无需通读每一份更新日志，就能快速浏览"有什么新东西，以及它对我意味着什么"。最新内容在前。 本页如何保持更新 条目由社区添加，也由一个 自动监测程序 标记上游变更，再交由人工撰写。每个条目都会链接其官方来源。发现有遗漏？添加它。
每条更新都按 领域 标记——🗣️ 应用（聊天/语音/移动端）、🛠️ Claude Code、🔌 API、🧠 模型——并回答 "它对你意味着什么"。

🧠 模型——Claude Sonnet 5 已于 2026 年 6 月 30 日发布，现在是 Claude Code 中的默认模型，具备原生 1M-token 上下文窗口，并在 August 31 2026 之前提供introductory 定价。它是全新的均衡型"从这里开始"Sonnet 层级，取代了 Claude Sonnet 4.6（现已成为旧版模型）。这意味着什么： 如果你固定使用某个模型，请迁移到 claude-sonnet-5；在依赖某篇博客文章中的数字之前，请始终查阅 当前模型与定价 表格，以获取确切的 ID 和实时定价。 最后验证时间：2026-07-01。 API ID claude-sonnet-5；Sonnet 层级；1M-token 上下文；128k 最大输出；2026 年 1 月知识截止。introductory 定价为每 MTok $2 / $10，适用至 Aug 31, 2026（标准价 $3 / $15）。根据更新日志（v2.1.197，June 30 2026），现为 Claude Code 默认模型。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 🛠️ Claude Code——**动态工作流（Dynamic workflows）**进入研究预览阶段：请求一个工作流（或设置 /effort ultracode），Claude 就会编写一段 JavaScript 脚本，在后台编排数十到数百个 子代理——用于全代码库审计、大型迁移以及交叉核验的研究。运行 /deep-research 查看内置示例，或运行 /workflows 观察运行情况。这意味着什么： 你现在可以承担单次对话永远无法协调的舰队级任务，并将编排过程保存为可重复运行的命令。参见 动态工作流与 ultracode。 最后验证时间：2026-06-24。 需要 Claude Code v2.1.154+；在付费计划、API、Bedrock、Vertex 和 Foundry 上均可用。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 🧠 模型——一款全新的顶级模型 Claude Fable 5 已于 2026 年 6 月发布（Claude Code v2.1.170+）。这意味着什么： 在固定使用某个模型之前，请查阅 当前模型与定价 表格，了解最新的阵容和确切 ID——切勿硬编码某篇博客文章中的模型信息。 🛠️ Claude Code——子代理现在可以生成它们自己的子代理（最多 5 层深），并且 /code-review --fix 会将审查结果应用到你的工作区。这意味着什么： 委派可以组合得更深入，审查也能形成闭环，而不仅仅是给出报告。请对照 官方更新日志 核实确切行为。 🔌 API——诸如结构化输出、扩展思考和提示缓存等能力在不断演进。这意味着什么： 在依赖确切参数之前，请重新查阅 API 章节。

复制为 Markdown 最后验证时间：2026-10-15。 训练截止日期取自 Claude Platform 文档中各模型的页面。Claude Code 文档的历史来自一个社区镜像，它每天多次复制官方页面。这些数字是 2026 年 10 月 15 日的快照；生成它们的脚本已在下方链接，任何人都可以重新运行。 请对照以下来源核实： 官方来源. 每个 Claude 模型都是从其训练截止日期时的文档中学会 Claude Code 的。此后文档仍在不断变化。我们按周回放了它的历史，以衡量两者已经相隔多远。 68% of what the official Claude Code docs said on 2026年10月15日 was not in them at the end of 2026年6月: the training cutoff of Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5. 最新的模型 Fable 5.1、Opus 5.5、Sonnet 5.5 和 Haiku 5.5 的可靠知识截止日期是 2026 年 6 月。从 6 月底到 10 月 15 日，文档从 107 页增长到 164 页，如今文档所说的大部分内容都写于这三个半月里。若按更严格的方式计算，即按确切措辞而非按事实，这一比例升至 72%。去掉代码示例则是 70%。无论怎么算，Claude 都从未见过自己手册的大部分内容。

documents.t: since-cutoff 插件会把这些清单放到 Claude 面前。会话启动时，一个 hook 读取正在运行的是哪个模型，并向其上下文添加一条简短的说明：在该模型截止日期之后才有文档记录的标志、命令和 hook 事件，以及一条指令——在依赖记忆或声称某功能不存在之前，先查阅文档。 claude plugin marketplace add derob98/ailmanac --sparse .claude-plugin plugins claude plugin install since-cutoff@ailmanac 这个 hook 只有几行 POSIX shell：不需要 Node，不联网，每个会话约 400 到 750 个 token。当 Claude Code 没有把模型传给 hook 时，例如在我们的无头 -p 测试中，说明会列出自 2026 年 6 月以来的变化，这对每个 Claude 模型都成立。在那次测试中，会话收到了说明，Claude 把它一字不差地复述了出来。

不要相信 Claude 对 Claude Code 的记忆。 对于标志、设置、hook 和命令，让它去读页面。Claude Code 自带一个回答自身问题的向导代理，文档也在 code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt 发布了索引。 给你的教程标注日期。 六个月前的指南已经失去了三分之一以上的事实。复制其中的命令之前，请对照文档检查任何更早的内容。 优先选择注明核实时间的页面。 本站每个页面都带有最后一次核实的日期；新鲜度仪表盘列出了所有页面，Deprecation & Migration Watch 则追踪被移除的内容。

历史。 web3dev1337/claude-code-docs 是一个知名文档镜像的分叉，保留了完整的同步历史：2025 年 7 月至 2026 年 10 月之间共 3,604 次同步。我们取每周的最后一次同步，共 67 份快照。 范围。 除变更日志和每周摘要（它们本来就是为记录历史而存在）以及 Agent SDK 页面（2026 年从另一个文档站点迁入，否则会被算作新增）之外的所有 Claude Code 页面。 单位。 每个页面被拆分为句子、表格行和代码行，去除链接和标记。同时出现在五个或更多页面上的行，例如横幅或通用代码行，会被丢弃。最终剩下 90,674 个不同的单位可供追踪。 消失。 一个单位在连续两份每周快照中缺失，或在最新一份快照中缺失，就算消失，因此某个页面在一次同步中失败不会被计入。 事实。 同一周内，替换了一句被删除句子的新句子，如果至少 60% 的词相同，且每个数字、标志、路径和标识符都完全一致，就被视为同一个事实。用这种方法关联了 7,965 处改写。 截止日期。 每个模型与其截止月份最后一天或之前的最后一份每周快照比较，这是最宽松的解读。早于 2025 年 7 月的截止日期使用第一份快照，而它包含的内容已经多于这些模型可能见过的内容：它们的占比是下限。 存活。 对第一份快照之后产生的所有单位做 Kaplan–Meier 估计，至今仍然存在的单位按删失处理。 这个镜像并非官方：如果它漏掉或弄乱了某个页面，数字也会随之带有偏差。我们检查了截止日期所在的几周，看是否有页面在一次同步中消失，没有发现。这项分析比较的是文本，而不是产品行为。

脚本及其输出都在本站的仓库中：scripts/research/docs-decay.mjs 和 data/research/claude-code-docs-decay.json。需要 Node 和 git，运行约 15 秒： git clone https://github.com/web3dev1337/claude-code-docs git clone https://github.com/derob98/ailmanac node ailmanac/scripts/research/docs-decay.mjs claude-code-docs 分享此页面 X LinkedIn Reddit Hacker News 复制链接
